Middle Test.prompt: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the _____ of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
Middle Test.verse: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
Middle Test.note: David's answer to Goliath: sword, spear, and shield on one side; a name on the other.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the _____. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
Middle Test.verse: And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
Middle Test.note: Nathan's four-word thunderclap to King David — the shortest sermon that ever landed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then went he down, and dipped himself _____ times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
Middle Test.verse: Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
Middle Test.note: Naaman wanted something grander, but the cure was seven dips in the muddy old Jordan.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; _____ be the name of the LORD.
Middle Test.verse: And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
Middle Test.note: Job's response to losing everything: 'blessed be the name of the LORD' — worship through tears.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Enter into his gates with _____, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
Middle Test.verse: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
Middle Test.note: The gate password is thanksgiving; praise gets you into the courts.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: I will praise thee; for I am _____ and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
Middle Test.verse: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
Middle Test.note: 'Fearfully and wonderfully made' — fearfully here means awe, not anxiety.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Pride goeth before _____, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
Middle Test.verse: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
Middle Test.note: Everyone quotes 'pride goeth before a fall,' but the KJV says destruction first — the fall comes in the second half.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as _____, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
Middle Test.verse: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
Middle Test.note: God's courtroom invitation: sins dyed scarlet, promised white as snow.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery _____, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.
Middle Test.verse: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.
Middle Test.note: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego's confidence: 'burning fiery furnace' — the KJV doubles down on the heat.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: My God hath sent his _____, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
Middle Test.verse: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
Middle Test.note: Daniel's morning report from the lions' den: God's angel worked the night shift.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Go ye therefore, and _____ all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
Middle Test.verse: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
Middle Test.note: Modern versions say 'make disciples,' but the KJV's Great Commission says 'teach all nations.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a _____; because there was no room for them in the inn.
Middle Test.verse: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
Middle Test.note: The Christmas verse: no room in the inn, so the King of kings got a feeding trough.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had _____, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
Middle Test.verse: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
Middle Test.note: The prodigal's father saw him 'a great way off' — which means he'd been watching the road.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: I am the _____, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
Middle Test.verse: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
Middle Test.note: The vine-and-branches math: abiding yields much fruit; without him, the total is nothing.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Neither is there _____ in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
Middle Test.verse: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
Middle Test.note: Peter before the council: one name under heaven, no backup options listed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And be not _____ to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
Middle Test.verse: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
Middle Test.note: Conformed is the world's mold; transformed is God's renovation — one letter swap, whole different life.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a _____ giver.
Middle Test.verse: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.
Middle Test.note: 'Not grudgingly, or of necessity' — God audits the attitude, not just the amount.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will _____ from you.
Middle Test.verse: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Middle Test.note: The promise is startlingly practical: resist, and the devil doesn't negotiate — he flees.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the LORD said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's _____?
Middle Test.verse: And the LORD said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?
Middle Test.note: Cain's deflection became the world's most famous rhetorical question — and the answer is yes.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a _____ for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
Middle Test.verse: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
Middle Test.note: Abraham's answer on Moriah: God will provide himself a lamb — a promise bigger than he knew.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many _____.
Middle Test.verse: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.
Middle Test.note: The KJV spells it 'colours' — the coat that launched a musical and a family feud.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the LORD said unto him, What is that in thine hand? And he said, A _____.
Middle Test.verse: And the LORD said unto him, What is that in thine hand? And he said, A rod.
Middle Test.note: God's question to Moses: what's already in your hand? A shepherd's rod, about to have a career.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will _____ over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.
Middle Test.verse: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.
Middle Test.note: The verse where Passover gets its name — the blood on the doorposts, and judgment passing over.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is _____: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.
Middle Test.verse: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.
Middle Test.note: 'Manna' is basically Hebrew for 'what is it?' — Israel named breakfast after their own confusion.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, _____; for the LORD hath given you the city.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the LORD hath given you the city.
Middle Test.note: Seven laps, seven trumpets, and then the one-word battle plan at Jericho: 'Shout.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then spake Joshua to the LORD in the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou _____ upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon.
Middle Test.verse: Then spake Joshua to the LORD in the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon.
Middle Test.note: Joshua's audacious battlefield prayer: 'Sun, stand thou still' — and the sun took orders.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Behold, I will put a fleece of wool in the floor; and if the _____ be on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the earth beside, then shall I know that thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said.
Middle Test.verse: Behold, I will put a fleece of wool in the floor; and if the dew be on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the earth beside, then shall I know that thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as thou hast said.
Middle Test.note: Gideon's famous fleece test: dew on the wool, dry ground everywhere else — sign requested, sign granted.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: That he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a _____ upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.
Middle Test.verse: That he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a razor upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.
Middle Test.note: Samson finally tells Delilah the secret: no razor, ever — and you can guess what she went shopping for.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and _____ ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. And she said unto her, Go, my daughter.
Middle Test.verse: And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. And she said unto her, Go, my daughter.
Middle Test.note: Gleaning was Israel's welfare law — leftovers at the field's edge, where Ruth met Boaz.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Eben-ezer, saying, Hitherto hath the LORD _____ us.
Middle Test.verse: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Eben-ezer, saying, Hitherto hath the LORD helped us.
Middle Test.note: The Ebenezer stone from the hymn — 'hitherto' is KJV for 'this far, every step.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five _____ stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.
Middle Test.verse: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.
Middle Test.note: Five smooth stones from the brook — David packed four more than he needed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And David _____ before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.
Middle Test.verse: And David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod.
Middle Test.note: The ark comes home and the king danced with all his might — dignity was not the priority.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Give therefore thy servant an _____ heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?
Middle Test.verse: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?
Middle Test.note: Offered anything, Solomon asked for an understanding heart — the request that pleased God.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the _____ brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.
Middle Test.verse: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.
Middle Test.note: Elijah's meal delivery at the brook Cherith came by raven — twice a day, no tips accepted.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the man of God said, Where fell it? And he shewed him the place. And he cut down a stick, and cast it in thither; and the iron did _____.
Middle Test.verse: And the man of God said, Where fell it? And he shewed him the place. And he cut down a stick, and cast it in thither; and the iron did swim.
Middle Test.note: A borrowed axe head lost in the river, and Elisha makes iron swim — small problems matter to God too.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I _____, I perish.
Middle Test.verse: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.
Middle Test.note: Esther's resolve before the unsummoned walk to the throne room: 'if I perish, I perish.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But Daniel _____ in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
Middle Test.verse: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
Middle Test.note: Daniel 'purposed in his heart' before the menu ever arrived — the decision preceded the test.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: In the same hour came forth _____ of a man's hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king's palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
Middle Test.verse: In the same hour came forth fingers of a man's hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king's palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
Middle Test.note: Belshazzar's feast, interrupted: the original writing on the wall, delivered in person.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become _____ of men.
Middle Test.verse: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
Middle Test.note: Jesus recruits from the docks: same nets, new catch — 'fishers of men.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the _____, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
Middle Test.verse: When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
Middle Test.note: The KJV says 'physician' where we'd say doctor — Jesus explaining why he keeps such company.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jesus answering said unto them, _____ to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. And they marvelled at him.
Middle Test.verse: And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. And they marvelled at him.
Middle Test.note: 'Render' is the KJV's word for 'give back' — Caesar's coin to Caesar, God's image to God.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into temptation. The spirit truly is _____, but the flesh is weak.
Middle Test.verse: Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.
Middle Test.note: Everyone quotes 'the spirit is willing,' but the KJV in Mark says the spirit truly is 'ready.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But God prepared a _____ when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered.
Middle Test.verse: But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered.
Middle Test.note: God prepared a gourd for Jonah's shade, then a worm to wither it — an object lesson about caring for the wrong things.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which the LORD said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the _____ of Saul's robe privily.
Middle Test.verse: And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which the LORD said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul's robe privily.
Middle Test.note: David could have killed Saul in the cave; instead he cut off the 'skirt' of the king's robe — and still felt guilty.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was _____ and wild honey.
Middle Test.verse: And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey.
Middle Test.note: John the Baptist's wardrobe and menu: camel's hair, a leathern girdle, and locusts with wild honey.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven _____, fatfleshed and well favoured; and they fed in a meadow:
Middle Test.verse: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fatfleshed and well favoured; and they fed in a meadow:
Middle Test.note: Pharaoh retells his dream to Joseph: seven fat 'kine' — old English for cows — soon to be eaten by seven lean ones.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he ran before, and climbed up into a _____ tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
Middle Test.verse: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
Middle Test.note: The KJV spells it 'sycomore' — a sturdy fig tree, perfect for a short tax collector named Zacchaeus.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been _____: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.
Middle Test.verse: And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.
Middle Test.note: Saul's sight returned when something like scales fell from his eyes — the source of the English idiom.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me _____.
Middle Test.verse: Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
Middle Test.note: Peter swore he'd never deny Jesus; the KJV's 'thrice' came true before the cock crowed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when they were come into the _____, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
Middle Test.verse: And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
Middle Test.note: By the time the wise men arrived, the KJV has the young child in a house — the manger scene was behind them.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he said unto them, Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth _____. And they could not in three days expound the riddle.
Middle Test.verse: And he said unto them, Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. And they could not in three days expound the riddle.
Middle Test.note: Samson's riddle came from a lion's carcass full of bees — impossible to guess unless you'd been there.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and _____ it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
Middle Test.verse: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
Middle Test.note: 'Slang' is the KJV's past tense of sling — one stone, one shot, and Goliath fell face first.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the king said, _____ the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.
Middle Test.verse: And the king said, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.
Middle Test.note: Solomon's famous ruling: threaten to split the baby, and the real mother reveals herself.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed _____.
Middle Test.verse: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
Middle Test.note: For Jesus' Jewish listeners, feeding swine was rock bottom — exactly where the prodigal son landed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jacob was left alone; and there _____ a man with him until the breaking of the day.
Middle Test.verse: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.
Middle Test.note: Jacob wrestled until daybreak and walked away with a limp and a new name: Israel.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live _____ in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar:
Middle Test.verse: Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar:
Middle Test.note: A seraph touched Isaiah's lips with a live coal from the altar — just before he answered, 'Here am I; send me.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Now the serpent was more _____ than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
Middle Test.verse: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
Middle Test.note: The KJV spells it 'subtil' — and the serpent opens Eden's first conversation by questioning what God really said.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a _____: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
Middle Test.verse: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
Middle Test.note: Mid-storm, Jesus was asleep on a pillow in the back of the boat — only Mark mentions the pillow.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive _____ pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
Middle Test.verse: And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.
Middle Test.note: The peace symbol says olive branch, but Noah's dove actually brought back an olive leaf, freshly 'pluckt off.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the three companies blew the trumpets, and brake the _____, and held the lamps in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands to blow withal: and they cried, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.
Middle Test.verse: And the three companies blew the trumpets, and brake the pitchers, and held the lamps in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands to blow withal: and they cried, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.
Middle Test.note: Gideon's 300 went to battle with trumpets, lamps, and breakable pitchers — the strangest arsenal in Israel's history.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not _____.
Middle Test.verse: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
Middle Test.note: The burning bush's real wonder wasn't the fire — it was that the bush was not consumed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup _____ over.
Middle Test.verse: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.
Middle Test.note: Psalm 23's banquet scene: a table set in front of the enemies, and a cup that runneth over.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And at _____ Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
Middle Test.verse: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
Middle Test.note: Beaten and locked in stocks, Paul and Silas held a midnight hymn sing — and the other prisoners were listening.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And forgive us our _____, as we forgive our debtors.
Middle Test.verse: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
Middle Test.note: Many congregations pray 'forgive us our trespasses,' but the KJV's Lord's Prayer in Matthew says debts.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of _____, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink.
Middle Test.verse: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink.
Middle Test.note: Baby Moses' basket is an 'ark' in the KJV, tucked among the bulrushes at the river's edge.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it _____ out Jonah upon the dry land.
Middle Test.verse: And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
Middle Test.note: Three days inside, then an unceremonious exit: the fish vomited Jonah out onto dry land.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in _____ clothes, lying in a manger.
Middle Test.verse: And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger.
Middle Test.note: The angel's sign for the shepherds: a newborn in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: In the sweat of thy _____ shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
Middle Test.verse: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
Middle Test.note: Everyone says 'by the sweat of your brow,' but the KJV puts the sweat on Adam's face.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten _____: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
Middle Test.verse: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
Middle Test.note: Aaron made a molten calf while Moses was up the mountain — later claiming it just came out of the fire.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was _____ with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
Middle Test.note: Jonathan, the king's son and heir, loved David as his own soul — one of the Bible's great friendships.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of _____.
Middle Test.verse: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
Middle Test.note: Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and became a pillar of salt — Jesus later warned simply, 'Remember Lot's wife.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a _____, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.
Middle Test.verse: Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.
Middle Test.note: A bushel was a grain-measuring basket — the one place you definitely shouldn't hide a lit candle.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third _____, and was taken up dead.
Middle Test.verse: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
Middle Test.note: Eutychus dozed off during Paul's long sermon and fell from the third loft — Paul revived him, then kept talking till dawn.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, _____ be thy name.
Middle Test.verse: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
Middle Test.note: 'Hallowed' means treated as holy — the Lord's Prayer honors God's name before making a single request.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own _____, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
Middle Test.verse: And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
Middle Test.note: The Good Samaritan set the wounded man on his own beast — the KJV never actually says donkey.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jesus increased in wisdom and _____, and in favour with God and man.
Middle Test.verse: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
Middle Test.note: Luke's summary of Jesus' quiet years in Nazareth: growth in wisdom, stature, and favour with God and man.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the _____ of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:
Middle Test.verse: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:
Middle Test.note: Jesus' cure for worry: look at the lilies, which neither toil nor spin and still outdress Solomon.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: The _____ also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.
Middle Test.verse: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.
Middle Test.note: Everyone remembers 'the lion shall lie down with the lamb,' but the KJV pairs the lamb with the wolf.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not _____, but believing.
Middle Test.verse: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.
Middle Test.note: The origin of 'doubting Thomas' — though the word Jesus actually uses in the KJV is faithless.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet _____ in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father's household, home unto thee.
Middle Test.verse: Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father's household, home unto thee.
Middle Test.note: Rahab's scarlet thread in the window marked the one household in Jericho that would be spared.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: After that he poureth water into a _____, and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded.
Middle Test.verse: After that he poureth water into a bason, and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded.
Middle Test.note: The KJV spells it 'bason' — the night Jesus took a towel and washed his disciples' feet.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Go to the ant, thou _____; consider her ways, and be wise:
Middle Test.verse: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:
Middle Test.note: Solomon's productivity seminar: one ant, no supervisor, and a lesson for every sluggard.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as _____, and so we were in their sight.
Middle Test.verse: And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.
Middle Test.note: Ten of the twelve spies saw giants and felt like grasshoppers — and that self-image cost Israel forty years.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a _____ out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
Middle Test.verse: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
Middle Test.note: Shipwrecked on Malta, Paul gathers firewood and a viper latches on — he shakes it into the fire, unharmed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a _____ unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
Middle Test.verse: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
Middle Test.note: Israel crossed the Red Sea on dry ground, the waters standing as a wall on their right hand and on their left.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: There is a _____ here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?
Middle Test.verse: There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?
Middle Test.note: The KJV calls him a lad — the boy whose five barley loaves and two small fishes fed five thousand.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and _____ of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.
Middle Test.verse: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.
Middle Test.note: Esau traded his birthright for 'pottage of lentiles' — history's most expensive bowl of lentil stew.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a _____ to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
Middle Test.verse: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
Middle Test.note: A camel through a needle's eye — Jesus' deliberately absurd picture, and the disciples were exceedingly amazed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and _____ up the water that was in the trench.
Middle Test.verse: Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.
Middle Test.note: On Mount Carmel the fire fell and even licked up the water Elijah had poured into the trench.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Make thee an ark of _____ wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
Middle Test.verse: Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
Middle Test.note: Gopher wood appears exactly once in the Bible, and nobody is quite sure what tree it was.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And why beholdest thou the _____ that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
Middle Test.verse: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
Middle Test.note: Modern versions say speck; the KJV says mote — while you ignore the beam, a whole plank, in your own eye.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a _____, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
Middle Test.verse: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
Middle Test.note: Moses lifted a serpent of brass on a pole — the very image Jesus later applied to himself in John 3.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Be ye therefore _____ of God, as dear children;
Middle Test.verse: Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children;
Middle Test.note: Modern versions say 'imitators' — Paul's picture is dear children copying the parent they love.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But she had brought them up to the roof of the house, and hid them with the stalks of _____, which she had laid in order upon the roof.
Middle Test.verse: But she had brought them up to the roof of the house, and hid them with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof.
Middle Test.note: Rahab hid Joshua's spies on her roof under stalks of flax laid out to dry — then sent the king's men off on a wild goose chase.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small _____ lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
Middle Test.verse: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
Middle Test.note: No sun, no stars, many days of tempest — just before Paul stood up and told everyone to be of good cheer.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his _____ was white as the light.
Middle Test.verse: And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
Middle Test.note: On the mount of transfiguration Jesus' face shone like the sun, and even his raiment turned white as the light.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two _____, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
Middle Test.verse: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
Middle Test.note: The Samaritan paid the innkeeper two pence and promised to cover the rest — mercy with an open tab.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: All the presidents of the kingdom, the governors, and the princes, the counsellors, and the captains, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a firm decree, that whosoever shall ask a _____ of any God or man for thirty days, save of thee, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.
Middle Test.verse: All the presidents of the kingdom, the governors, and the princes, the counsellors, and the captains, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a firm decree, that whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of thee, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.
Middle Test.note: The trap for Daniel: no petition to any god or man but the king for thirty days — or into the lions' den.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And there were in the same country shepherds _____ in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.
Middle Test.verse: And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.
Middle Test.note: The first Christmas announcement went to night-shift shepherds, abiding in the field with their flock.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would _____ him of his leprosy.
Middle Test.verse: And she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.
Middle Test.note: A captive Israelite servant girl pointed her master Naaman to the prophet who could heal his leprosy.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And after a time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcase of the lion: and, behold, there was a swarm of _____ and honey in the carcase of the lion.
Middle Test.verse: And after a time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcase of the lion: and, behold, there was a swarm of bees and honey in the carcase of the lion.
Middle Test.note: Back at the lion's carcass, Samson found a swarm of bees and honey — the secret behind his famous riddle.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: He opened the _____, and the waters gushed out; they ran in the dry places like a river.
Middle Test.verse: He opened the rock, and the waters gushed out; they ran in the dry places like a river.
Middle Test.note: The psalm remembers Moses' rock: God opened it, and water ran through the desert like a river.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his _____.
Middle Test.verse: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.
Middle Test.note: Joseph's dying wish was to have his bones carried out of Egypt — and Moses kept the promise (Exodus 13:19).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the _____ of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.
Middle Test.verse: And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.
Middle Test.note: John is told to look at the Lion of Juda — and when he turns, he sees a Lamb (Revelation 5:6).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the _____ of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.
Middle Test.verse: And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.
Middle Test.note: God came walking in the garden in the cool of the day — and for the first time, his people hid instead of meeting him.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt _____ the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
Middle Test.verse: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
Middle Test.note: At Horeb, God said strike the rock; years later at Meribah he said speak to it — and the difference mattered.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Boaz said unto her, At mealtime come thou hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the _____. And she sat beside the reapers: and he reached her parched corn, and she did eat, and was sufficed, and left.
Middle Test.verse: And Boaz said unto her, At mealtime come thou hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar. And she sat beside the reapers: and he reached her parched corn, and she did eat, and was sufficed, and left.
Middle Test.note: Lunch with Boaz: bread dipped in vinegar and parched corn — Ruth ate her fill and had leftovers to take home.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the LORD said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become _____ throughout all the land of Egypt.
Middle Test.verse: And the LORD said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
Middle Test.note: Modern versions often say gnats; the KJV says lice — the plague where Pharaoh's magicians finally admitted, 'This is the finger of God.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an _____ to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.
Middle Test.verse: By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.
Middle Test.note: Noah built the ark after being warned of 'things not seen as yet' — faith in a forecast nobody else believed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the barbarous people shewed us no little _____: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
Middle Test.verse: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
Middle Test.note: Shipwrecked and soaked, Paul's company found the islanders of Melita showed 'no little kindness' — and lit a fire.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the _____ person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;
Middle Test.verse: And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;
Middle Test.note: Peter calls Noah 'the eighth person' — one of eight saved on the ark — and a preacher of righteousness.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers, and _____ within the pitchers.
Middle Test.verse: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers, and lamps within the pitchers.
Middle Test.note: Three hundred men, each with a trumpet and a lamp hidden in an empty pitcher — Gideon's whole battle plan.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the _____ of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
Middle Test.verse: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
Middle Test.note: While the sailors prayed and tossed cargo overboard, Jonah was fast asleep down in the sides of the ship.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: In Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a _____ by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.
Middle Test.verse: In Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.
Middle Test.note: At Gibeon, God appeared to young Solomon in a dream with a blank check: 'Ask what I shall give thee.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be _____.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.
Middle Test.note: The Christmas story starts with paperwork: Caesar's decree that 'all the world should be taxed' sent Joseph to Bethlehem.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and _____ them beneath the mount.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.
Middle Test.note: The KJV says 'brake' — Moses saw the calf and dancing and shattered the tablets at the mountain's foot.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they that went before, and they that followed, cried, saying, _____; Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord:
Middle Test.verse: And they that went before, and they that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna; Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord:
Middle Test.note: 'Hosanna' is a Hebrew cry meaning 'save now' — the Palm Sunday crowd shouting a prayer and a welcome at once.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my _____.
Middle Test.verse: So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
Middle Test.note: Breakfast on the beach, then a question for Peter — and a job: 'Feed my lambs.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Is not this the _____, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.
Middle Test.verse: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.
Middle Test.note: Nazareth shrugged him off as the local carpenter — Mark is the only Gospel that gives Jesus himself that title.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Moreover his mother made him a little _____, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
Middle Test.verse: Moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
Middle Test.note: Every year Hannah made young Samuel a little coat and brought it when she came up to the yearly sacrifice.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the _____ of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
Middle Test.verse: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
Middle Test.note: King Darius threw Daniel to the lions against his own wishes — and still told him his God would deliver him.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And your feet _____ with the preparation of the gospel of peace;
Middle Test.verse: And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace;
Middle Test.note: 'Shod' means wearing shoes — in the armour of God, your footwear is the gospel of peace.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And David sat between the two gates: and the _____ went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.
Middle Test.verse: And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.
Middle Test.note: David waited between the gates for news of the battle while the watchman scanned the road from the roof.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And a certain man lame from his mother's womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called _____, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple;
Middle Test.verse: And a certain man lame from his mother's womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple;
Middle Test.note: A lame man begged daily at the temple gate called Beautiful — until Peter offered something better than alms.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: That at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, _____, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up:
Middle Test.verse: That at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up:
Middle Test.note: The royal band's roster appears four times in Daniel 3, sackbut and all — the cue for everyone to bow to the image.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his _____ filled the temple.
Middle Test.verse: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
Middle Test.note: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord enthroned, his robe's train filling the whole temple.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And I turned to see the voice that spake with me. And being turned, I saw seven golden _____;
Middle Test.verse: And I turned to see the voice that spake with me. And being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks;
Middle Test.note: John turned to see who was speaking and saw seven golden candlesticks — the seven churches (Revelation 1:20).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his _____ fell off from his hands.
Middle Test.verse: And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
Middle Test.note: An angel woke Peter in prison with a smite on the side, and his chains simply fell off his hands.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden _____, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
Middle Test.verse: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
Middle Test.note: The KJV's 'cherubims' doubles up the plural — cherub plus Hebrew -im plus English -s — guarding Eden's gate with a flaming sword.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Greet all the brethren with an holy _____.
Middle Test.verse: Greet all the brethren with an holy kiss.
Middle Test.note: Paul's closing instruction: greet the brethren with an holy kiss — he says it in four different letters.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and _____ write unto thee:
Middle Test.verse: I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee:
Middle Test.note: John had more to say but preferred talking face to face over ink and pen.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jonathan stripped himself of the _____ that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.
Middle Test.verse: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.
Middle Test.note: Jonathan, heir to the throne, gave David his robe, sword, and bow — handing over the prince's things to his friend.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he found a new _____ of an ass, and put forth his hand, and took it, and slew a thousand men therewith.
Middle Test.verse: And he found a new jawbone of an ass, and put forth his hand, and took it, and slew a thousand men therewith.
Middle Test.note: Samson's weapon of choice was a fresh jawbone of a donkey — he even wrote a little victory poem about it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on _____, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
Middle Test.verse: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
Middle Test.note: One reluctant sermon, and all Nineveh put on sackcloth — from the greatest of them to the least.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: _____ thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)
Middle Test.verse: Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)
Middle Test.note: Paul notes that 'Honour thy father and mother' is the first commandment that comes with a promise attached.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of _____.
Middle Test.verse: His legs of iron, his feet part of iron and part of clay.
Middle Test.note: The statue in Nebuchadnezzar's dream had a golden head — and feet of iron mixed with clay. Not a sturdy base.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: He riseth from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a _____, and girded himself.
Middle Test.verse: He riseth from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a towel, and girded himself.
Middle Test.note: The King of kings rose from supper, laid aside his garments, and picked up a servant's towel.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But when he saw the wind _____, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.
Middle Test.verse: But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.
Middle Test.note: Peter was doing fine on the water until he noticed the wind was boisterous — then the sinking started.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the third day there was a _____ in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:
Middle Test.verse: And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:
Middle Test.note: Jesus' first miracle happened at a wedding in Cana — the KJV calls it a marriage, and the wine was about to run out.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Let the royal apparel be brought which the king useth to wear, and the _____ that the king rideth upon, and the crown royal which is set upon his head:
Middle Test.verse: Let the royal apparel be brought which the king useth to wear, and the horse that the king rideth upon, and the crown royal which is set upon his head:
Middle Test.note: Haman designed a royal parade thinking it was for himself — robe, crown, and the king's own horse. It was for Mordecai.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he took him a _____ to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.
Middle Test.verse: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.
Middle Test.note: Stripped of everything, Job sat in the ashes scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much _____?
Middle Test.verse: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
Middle Test.note: Jonah ends with God's question about Nineveh's people — and 'also much cattle.' He cared about the animals too.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Are not Abana and Pharpar, _____ of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.
Middle Test.verse: Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.
Middle Test.note: Naaman was insulted: Damascus had better rivers than the muddy Jordan — why dip in that?

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And a certain man drew a bow at a _____, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thine hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
Middle Test.verse: And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Israel between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thine hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
Middle Test.note: A soldier drew his bow 'at a venture' — at random — and the disguised king of Israel couldn't hide from it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: All the king's servants, and the people of the king's provinces, do know, that whosoever, whether man or woman, shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, there is one law of his to put him to death, except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden _____, that he may live: but I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.
Middle Test.verse: All the king's servants, and the people of the king's provinces, do know, that whosoever, whether man or woman, shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, there is one law of his to put him to death, except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live: but I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.
Middle Test.note: Approaching the king uninvited meant death — unless he held out the golden sceptre. Esther had not been called in thirty days.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the _____ of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
Middle Test.verse: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
Middle Test.note: At Zarephath's gate Elijah found a widow gathering sticks — and asked her, of all people, for a meal.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my _____.
Middle Test.verse: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.
Middle Test.note: The origin of 'by the skin of my teeth' — Job, describing how barely he'd escaped.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And as the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal Saul's daughter looked through a _____, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.
Middle Test.verse: And as the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal Saul's daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.
Middle Test.note: Michal watched from a window as David leaped and danced before the ark — and she was not a fan.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was _____, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.
Middle Test.verse: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.
Middle Test.note: The youngest son, called in from the sheep: ruddy, with a beautiful countenance — and God said, 'This is he.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Came behind him, and touched the _____ of his garment: and immediately her issue of blood stanched.
Middle Test.verse: Came behind him, and touched the border of his garment: and immediately her issue of blood stanched.
Middle Test.note: She only touched the border of his garment in a crowd — and Jesus still stopped to ask who touched him.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So they ran both together: and the other disciple did _____ Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.
Middle Test.verse: So they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.
Middle Test.note: On Easter morning two disciples raced to the tomb, and John's Gospel records that the other disciple won.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto _____: and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four beasts full of eyes before and behind.
Middle Test.verse: And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal: and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four beasts full of eyes before and behind.
Middle Test.note: John's view of heaven's throne room includes a sea of glass, clear as crystal.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Noah began to be an _____, and he planted a vineyard:
Middle Test.verse: And Noah began to be an husbandman, and he planted a vineyard:
Middle Test.note: 'Husbandman' is the KJV's word for farmer — Noah stepped off the ark and went straight back to working the ground.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that _____, and the tables of the covenant;
Middle Test.verse: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
Middle Test.note: Inside the ark of the covenant: the tables, a pot of manna, and Aaron's rod that budded (Numbers 17:8).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So David took the spear and the _____ of water from Saul's bolster; and they gat them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the LORD was fallen upon them.
Middle Test.verse: So David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster; and they gat them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the LORD was fallen upon them.
Middle Test.note: David crept into Saul's camp and left with the king's spear and water cruse — proof he could have struck, and didn't.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Josiah was _____ years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty and one years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath.
Middle Test.verse: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty and one years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath.
Middle Test.note: Josiah became king at eight years old — and grew up to lead one of Judah's greatest revivals.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were _____ afraid.
Middle Test.verse: And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid.
Middle Test.note: 'Sore afraid' is KJV for terrified — an angel plus the glory of the Lord will do that to a shepherd.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And I will shoot three _____ on the side thereof, as though I shot at a mark.
Middle Test.verse: And I will shoot three arrows on the side thereof, as though I shot at a mark.
Middle Test.note: Jonathan's secret signal for David hiding in the field: where the arrows landed would tell him whether to run.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he would have rent a _____, and he had nothing in his hand: but he told not his father or his mother what he had done.
Middle Test.verse: And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand: but he told not his father or his mother what he had done.
Middle Test.note: A young lion roared at Samson, and he rent it as easily as a young goat — then told neither father nor mother.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Saul armed David with his _____, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.
Middle Test.verse: And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.
Middle Test.note: Saul lent David his own armour and helmet — David tried walking in it and politely gave it all back.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Ye are our _____ written in our hearts, known and read of all men:
Middle Test.verse: Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men:
Middle Test.note: Paul tells the Corinthians they are his letter of recommendation — written on hearts, read by everyone.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was _____ cubits and a span.
Middle Test.verse: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
Middle Test.note: Goliath stood six cubits and a span tall — over nine feet by the usual reckoning.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained _____ in the sight of all them that looked upon her.
Middle Test.verse: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. And Esther obtained favour in the sight of all them that looked upon her.
Middle Test.note: Esther asked for nothing beyond what the chamberlain advised — and won favour with everyone who saw her.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they brought the _____ to Jesus, and cast their garments on him; and he sat upon him.
Middle Test.verse: And they brought the colt to Jesus, and cast their garments on him; and he sat upon him.
