Middle Test.note: The Palm Sunday ride: Mark calls it a colt, one that no man had ever sat on (Mark 11:2).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will _____ bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.
Middle Test.verse: Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.
Middle Test.note: God promises to 'rain bread from heaven' — the first announcement of manna.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Judah is a lion's _____: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?
Middle Test.verse: Judah is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?
Middle Test.note: Jacob's blessing calls Judah a lion's whelp — and Revelation 5:5 later hails 'the Lion of the tribe of Juda.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of _____, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.
Middle Test.verse: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.
Middle Test.note: Lydia, a seller of purple from Thyatira, opened her heart to Paul's message — and then her home (Acts 16:15).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee _____. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.
Middle Test.verse: And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.
Middle Test.note: 'Thy faith hath made thee whole' — and the first thing Bartimaeus did with his new sight was follow Jesus.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And if thou refuse to let them go, behold, I will smite all thy borders with _____:
Middle Test.verse: And if thou refuse to let them go, behold, I will smite all thy borders with frogs:
Middle Test.note: The plague of frogs reached ovens, beds, and kneading troughs — and Pharaoh, asked when they should go, said 'To morrow.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the staff of his spear was like a weaver's _____; and his spear's head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and one bearing a shield went before him.
Middle Test.verse: And the staff of his spear was like a weaver's beam; and his spear's head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and one bearing a shield went before him.
Middle Test.note: Goliath's spear shaft was like a weaver's beam — the giant came armed with what looked like a loom part.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: I John, who also am your brother, and companion in tribulation, and in the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ, was in the _____ that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ.
Middle Test.verse: I John, who also am your brother, and companion in tribulation, and in the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ, was in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ.
Middle Test.note: John received his Revelation in exile on the isle called Patmos, 'for the word of God.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And if a house be _____ against itself, that house cannot stand.
Middle Test.verse: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
Middle Test.note: Lincoln borrowed it in 1858; Jesus first said it to critics who claimed he cast out devils by the devil's power.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king's words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and _____. So they strengthened their hands for this good work.
Middle Test.verse: Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king's words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for this good work.
Middle Test.note: Nehemiah's pep talk worked: the people answered, 'Let us rise up and build' — and the wall went up in 52 days.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he saith unto me, Write, Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage _____ of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of God.
Middle Test.verse: And he saith unto me, Write, Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of God.
Middle Test.note: Revelation's best invitation: blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a _____; and Moses fled from before it.
Middle Test.verse: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
Middle Test.note: Moses' shepherd rod hit the ground as a serpent — and the future deliverer of Israel ran from it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass, when the sun did arise, that God prepared a _____ east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and wished in himself to die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass, when the sun did arise, that God prepared a vehement east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and wished in himself to die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.
Middle Test.note: First the gourd withered, then a vehement east wind and a beating sun — and Jonah asked to die over it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his _____.
Middle Test.verse: By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.
Middle Test.note: Jacob's final act of faith: blessing Joseph's two sons, and worshipping as he leaned on the top of his staff.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, I had three white _____ on my head:
Middle Test.verse: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, I had three white baskets on my head:
Middle Test.note: The chief baker's dream had three white baskets on his head — and Joseph's reading of it was not the good news he hoped for.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses on the day we came forth to go unto you; but now, behold, it is dry, and it is _____:
Middle Test.verse: This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses on the day we came forth to go unto you; but now, behold, it is dry, and it is mouldy:
Middle Test.note: The Gibeonites' trick: show off mouldy bread as 'proof' of a long journey — and Israel didn't ask God first.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he _____: for he hath been dead four days.
Middle Test.verse: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days.
Middle Test.note: Practical Martha objected to opening Lazarus' tomb: four days in, 'he stinketh' — the KJV doesn't sugarcoat it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Yet Michael the _____, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee.
Middle Test.verse: Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee.
Middle Test.note: Even Michael the archangel wouldn't trade insults with the devil — he just said, 'The Lord rebuke thee.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him _____.
Middle Test.verse: And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
Middle Test.note: Zacchaeus' repentance came with numbers: half his goods to the poor, and fourfold to anyone he had cheated.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Pharaoh took off his _____ from his hand, and put it upon Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;
Middle Test.verse: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;
Middle Test.note: From prison to palace in one day: Pharaoh's own ring, fine linen, and a gold chain for the dream interpreter.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And one went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered thereof wild _____ his lap full, and came and shred them into the pot of pottage: for they knew them not.
Middle Test.verse: And one went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered thereof wild gourds his lap full, and came and shred them into the pot of pottage: for they knew them not.
Middle Test.note: A well-meaning cook shredded wild gourds into the prophets' stew — and the next verse finds out why that was a mistake.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Meekness, _____: against such there is no law.
Middle Test.verse: Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
Middle Test.note: The fruit of the Spirit ends with meekness and temperance — self-control — and there's no law against any of it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and _____ bones received strength.
Middle Test.verse: And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ancle bones received strength.
Middle Test.note: The KJV spells it 'ancle' — and the lame man's feet and ancle bones got strong enough to leap.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been _____.
Middle Test.verse: Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken.
Middle Test.note: Hannah prayed so silently and earnestly that Eli assumed she'd been drinking — it was the opposite.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the people took their _____ before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.
Middle Test.verse: And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.
Middle Test.note: Israel left so fast the bread never rose — they carried the dough out on their shoulders, kneading troughs and all.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Samson took hold of the two middle _____ upon which the house stood, and on which it was borne up, of the one with his right hand, and of the other with his left.
Middle Test.verse: And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house stood, and on which it was borne up, of the one with his right hand, and of the other with his left.
Middle Test.note: Samson's last act: two middle pillars, one in each hand, and the Philistine temple came down.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: The mountains _____ like rams, and the little hills like lambs.
Middle Test.verse: The mountains skipped like rams, and the little hills like lambs.
Middle Test.note: When Israel came out of Egypt, the psalmist says the mountains skipped like rams and the hills like lambs.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by _____ land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.
Middle Test.verse: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned.
Middle Test.note: The Red Sea crossing in one line: Israel walked through on dry land; the Egyptians tried it and drowned.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the soldiers _____ a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe,
Middle Test.verse: And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe,
Middle Test.note: The KJV spells it 'platted' — the soldiers wove a crown of thorns and added a purple robe to mock the King.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four _____ out of the stern, and wished for the day.
Middle Test.verse: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
Middle Test.note: On Paul's shipwreck voyage the sailors dropped four anchors from the stern and 'wished for the day.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white _____; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.
Middle Test.verse: And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.
Middle Test.note: Heaven opens and a white horse appears, its rider called Faithful and True.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Do thy diligence to come before _____. Eubulus greeteth thee, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brethren.
Middle Test.verse: Do thy diligence to come before winter. Eubulus greeteth thee, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brethren.
Middle Test.note: Paul, a prisoner, asks Timothy to hurry and 'come before winter' — perhaps he wanted that cloke.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And ere the _____ of God went out in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was, and Samuel was laid down to sleep;
Middle Test.verse: And ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was, and Samuel was laid down to sleep;
Middle Test.note: Before the lamp of God went out, young Samuel was asleep in the temple — and about to hear his name called.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in _____, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.
Middle Test.verse: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.
Middle Test.note: The KJV spells it 'morter' — Israel's lives made bitter with brick and mortar under Egypt's taskmasters.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: The king spake, and said, Is not this great Babylon, that I have _____ for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?
Middle Test.verse: The king spake, and said, Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?
Middle Test.note: Nebuchadnezzar's boast — 'great Babylon, that I have built' — was still in his mouth when the humbling came.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: On the morrow, as they went on their journey, and drew nigh unto the city, Peter went up upon the _____ to pray about the sixth hour:
Middle Test.verse: On the morrow, as they went on their journey, and drew nigh unto the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour:
Middle Test.note: Peter went up on the housetop to pray, got hungry, and received a vision that was all about food.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when he had agreed with the labourers for a _____ a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
Middle Test.verse: And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
Middle Test.note: The KJV's 'penny' was a denarius, a day's wage — and in this parable the latecomers got paid the very same.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became _____ unto it.
Middle Test.verse: And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it.
Middle Test.note: Bitter Naomi ends the book with a baby in her lap — Obed, who would become King David's grandfather.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a _____ child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.
Middle Test.verse: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.
Middle Test.note: Moses' parents hid him three months because they saw he was a 'proper child' — the KJV's word for a fine baby.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Let us make a little _____, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall be, when he cometh to us, that he shall turn in thither.
Middle Test.verse: Let us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall be, when he cometh to us, that he shall turn in thither.
Middle Test.note: The Shunammite couple built Elisha a little room on the wall: a bed, table, stool, and candlestick.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride _____ for her husband.
Middle Test.verse: And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
Middle Test.note: The new Jerusalem comes down from heaven 'as a bride adorned for her husband' — heaven's grand entrance.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all that night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the _____.
Middle Test.verse: And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all that night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.
Middle Test.note: An east wind all day and all night, and by morning the locusts arrived — then a west wind blew them into the Red Sea.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And many spread their _____ in the way: and others cut down branches off the trees, and strawed them in the way.
Middle Test.verse: And many spread their garments in the way: and others cut down branches off the trees, and strawed them in the way.
Middle Test.note: The crowd paved the road with their own garments and cut branches — a red carpet, Jerusalem style.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying _____.
Middle Test.verse: And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle.
Middle Test.note: Heaven's four creatures: a lion, a calf, a man's face, and a flying eagle — Ezekiel saw them too (Ezekiel 1:10).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the _____.
Middle Test.verse: Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.
Middle Test.note: The servants filled the waterpots to the brim — and by the time it was drawn out, the water had become good wine.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than _____, they were stronger than lions.
Middle Test.verse: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
Middle Test.note: David's lament for Saul and Jonathan: swifter than eagles, stronger than lions, and not divided in death.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his _____. And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle.
Middle Test.verse: And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle.
Middle Test.note: God spoke with Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his friend — while young Joshua never left the tent.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the city lieth _____, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.
Middle Test.verse: And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.
Middle Test.note: The new Jerusalem lies foursquare — its length, breadth, and height all equal.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And she put the _____ of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck:
Middle Test.verse: And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck:
Middle Test.note: Rebekah's costume department: goatskins on Jacob's hands to pass for hairy Esau before his blind father.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And she made him sleep upon her _____; and she called for a man, and she caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.
Middle Test.verse: And she made him sleep upon her knees; and she called for a man, and she caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.
Middle Test.note: Modern versions say 'lap'; the KJV has Delilah lull Samson to sleep upon her knees before calling for the barber.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about _____ furlongs.
Middle Test.verse: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs.
Middle Test.note: Threescore furlongs is about seven miles — the Emmaus road walk where a stranger turned out to be Jesus.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And thou shalt write them upon the _____ of thy house, and on thy gates.
Middle Test.verse: And thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates.
Middle Test.note: Write God's words on the posts of your house and your gates — faith meant to be seen coming and going.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he had an _____ of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
Middle Test.verse: And he had an helmet of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
Middle Test.note: Goliath's gear: a brass helmet and a coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels — he dressed for a much longer fight.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But Jehoiada the priest took a _____, and bored a hole in the lid of it, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one cometh into the house of the LORD: and the priests that kept the door put therein all the money that was brought into the house of the LORD.
Middle Test.verse: But Jehoiada the priest took a chest, and bored a hole in the lid of it, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one cometh into the house of the LORD: and the priests that kept the door put therein all the money that was brought into the house of the LORD.
Middle Test.note: Jehoiada bored a hole in a chest's lid for temple repair money — a priestly offering box.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the _____, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick:
Middle Test.verse: We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick:
Middle Test.note: Free fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, garlic — Israel waxing nostalgic about Egypt's menu and forgetting the slavery.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no _____, no bread, no money in their purse:
Middle Test.verse: And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse:
Middle Test.note: A scrip was a traveller's bag — Jesus sent the twelve out with a staff and not much else.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So that from his body were brought unto the sick _____ or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
Middle Test.verse: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
Middle Test.note: Even Paul's handkerchiefs and aprons carried healing in Ephesus — the most unusual laundry in Acts.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the _____:
Middle Test.verse: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand:
Middle Test.note: The foolish builder heard the very same sermon; his only mistake was not doing it — and great was the fall.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a _____ mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
Middle Test.verse: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
Middle Test.note: Pentecost began with a sound from heaven like a rushing mighty wind, filling the whole house.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the _____ that springeth out of the wall: he spake also of beasts, and of fowl, and of creeping things, and of fishes.
Middle Test.verse: And he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall: he spake also of beasts, and of fowl, and of creeping things, and of fishes.
Middle Test.note: Solomon lectured on everything from the mighty cedar to the humble hyssop growing out of a wall.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And she dwelt under the _____ tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.
Middle Test.verse: And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.
Middle Test.note: Deborah held court under a palm tree in the hills of Ephraim — Israel's only woman judge, with an outdoor office.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when he had made a _____ of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers' money, and overthrew the tables;
Middle Test.verse: And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers' money, and overthrew the tables;
Middle Test.note: John's temple scene: Jesus made a scourge of small cords and drove out the sheep, the oxen, and the changers.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the _____, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
Middle Test.note: The KJV's 'doctors' were teachers of the law — and twelve-year-old Jesus sat among them asking questions.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: His head and his hairs were white like _____, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire;
Middle Test.verse: His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire;
Middle Test.note: John's description of Jesus echoes Daniel 7:9: hair white like wool, as white as snow.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an _____.
Middle Test.verse: And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb.
Middle Test.note: Proof the risen Jesus wasn't a spirit: he ate broiled fish in front of them — and the KJV adds a honeycomb.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Took branches of _____ trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
Middle Test.verse: Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
Middle Test.note: Palm Sunday gets its name from this verse — only John says the crowd's branches came from palm trees.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Behold, we put _____ in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
Middle Test.verse: Behold, we put bits in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
Middle Test.note: James' tongue lesson: a small bit steers a whole horse — and a small tongue steers a whole life.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the _____ with his couch into the midst before Jesus.
Middle Test.verse: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus.
Middle Test.note: Luke's version of the roof story: the friends lowered the sick man through the tiling, couch and all, right before Jesus.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there _____ round about him a light from heaven:
Middle Test.verse: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:
Middle Test.note: On the Damascus road a light from heaven 'shined' round about Saul — the KJV doesn't say shone.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he hath on his _____ and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.
Middle Test.verse: And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.
Middle Test.note: The rider's vesture bears the title KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS — the words Handel's Hallelujah Chorus made famous.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish _____, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it.
Middle Test.verse: When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it.
Middle Test.note: Achan's confession: a goodly Babylonish garment, some silver, a wedge of gold — 'I coveted them, and took them.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Isaiah the prophet cried unto the LORD: and he brought the _____ ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz.
Middle Test.verse: And Isaiah the prophet cried unto the LORD: and he brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz.
Middle Test.note: Hezekiah's sign of healing: the shadow went backward ten degrees on the dial of Ahaz.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: The elder unto the elect _____ and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth;
Middle Test.verse: The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth;
Middle Test.note: John addresses this little letter to 'the elect lady and her children' — perhaps a woman, perhaps a whole church.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Ye see how _____ a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand.
Middle Test.verse: Ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand.
Middle Test.note: Near the end of Galatians, Paul takes up the pen himself — 'how large a letter I have written... with mine own hand.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Moses said, I will now turn _____, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
Middle Test.verse: And Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
Middle Test.note: Moses' curiosity started it all: he turned aside to look, and God spoke from the bush (Exodus 3:4).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard _____.
Middle Test.verse: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.
Middle Test.note: The queen of Sheba came to test Solomon with hard questions — and by the end 'there was no more spirit in her.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: The _____ are a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer;
Middle Test.verse: The ants are a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer;
Middle Test.note: Small but smart: the ants aren't strong, yet they stock up their food in summer.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the _____ of righteousness;
Middle Test.verse: Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness;
Middle Test.note: The armour of God: truth as the belt, righteousness as the breastplate — a Sunday school costume with a point.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou _____: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.
Middle Test.verse: Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.
Middle Test.note: Mark notes Jesus looked at the rich man and loved him — before naming the one thing he lacked.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the _____, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth.
Middle Test.note: King Jehoiakim sliced up Jeremiah's scroll with a penknife and fed it to the fire — so Jeremiah dictated it again.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a _____.
Middle Test.verse: For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall.
Middle Test.note: David's victory song: by God's help he could run through a troop and leap over a wall.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make _____ of skins, and clothed them.
Middle Test.verse: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them.
Middle Test.note: Before sending them out, God himself made Adam and Eve coats of skins — an upgrade from fig-leaf aprons.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to _____.
Middle Test.verse: Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality.
Middle Test.note: Paul's short list of Christian habits includes this one: 'given to hospitality' — keep the door open.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock _____.
Middle Test.verse: Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.
Middle Test.note: 'Crew' is the old past tense of crow — Peter's third denial and the rooster's timing were exactly as Jesus foretold.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Children, obey your _____ in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord.
Middle Test.verse: Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord.
Middle Test.note: The children's memory verse comes with a bonus line: obeying your parents is 'well pleasing unto the Lord.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of _____,
Middle Test.verse: Who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
Middle Test.note: A nod to Daniel among Hebrews' heroes of faith: those who 'stopped the mouths of lions.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared _____ and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king's meat.
Middle Test.verse: And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king's meat.
Middle Test.note: Ten days of vegetables and water, and Daniel's crew looked fairer and healthier than everyone eating the king's food.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river's side; and when she saw the ark among the _____, she sent her maid to fetch it.
Middle Test.verse: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river's side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.
Middle Test.note: The KJV says 'flags' for reeds — Pharaoh's daughter spotted the little ark tucked among them while going down to bathe.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the sun stood still, and the _____ stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day.
Middle Test.verse: And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day.
Middle Test.note: The sun stood still and the moon stayed — a day so long the Bible cites the book of Jasher as a second witness.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he would fain have filled his belly with the _____ that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
Middle Test.verse: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
Middle Test.note: The prodigal son hit bottom wishing he could eat the pigs' husks — and nobody gave him even that.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, _____ I was blind, now I see.
Middle Test.verse: He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
Middle Test.note: The healed man couldn't win a theology debate, but he had one unbeatable argument: 'whereas I was blind, now I see.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Let no corrupt _____ proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.
Middle Test.verse: Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.
Middle Test.note: 'Corrupt communication' is KJV for rotten talk — Paul's rule is only words that build people up.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith Abel offered unto God a more _____ sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
Middle Test.verse: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
Middle Test.note: Abel's offering was 'more excellent' than Cain's — and Hebrews says Abel, though dead, still speaks.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called _____, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth,
Middle Test.verse: And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth,
Middle Test.note: God gave Ananias an actual street address for Saul: the street called Straight, at the house of Judas.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band of men; and they cast the man into the sepulchre of Elisha: and when the man was let down, and touched the _____ of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band of men; and they cast the man into the sepulchre of Elisha: and when the man was let down, and touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet.
Middle Test.note: Even after his death, Elisha's bones brought a man back to life — a miracle-worker to the very end.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And through a _____ in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.
Middle Test.verse: And through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.
Middle Test.note: Paul's escape from Damascus in his own words: let down through a window in a basket over the wall (Acts 9:25).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and _____ which she did.
Middle Test.verse: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.
Middle Test.note: Dorcas was known for good works and almsdeeds — including the coats and garments the widows showed Peter.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they _____ left their nets, and followed him.
Middle Test.verse: And they straightway left their nets, and followed him.
Middle Test.note: 'Straightway' is the KJV's 'immediately' — Peter and Andrew left their nets on the spot and followed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many _____.
Middle Test.verse: And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many waters.
Middle Test.note: John hears the risen Jesus' voice as the sound of many waters — think a thundering waterfall.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe _____. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children.
Middle Test.verse: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children.
Middle Test.note: Baby Moses cried at the perfect moment — and the princess's heart melted, even knowing he was a Hebrew child.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, _____ to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter;
Middle Test.verse: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter;
Middle Test.note: Raised as royalty, Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter and stood with his own people.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and _____ the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.
Middle Test.verse: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.
Middle Test.note: In KJV English 'tell' means count — God hands Abram an impossible counting assignment to show the size of the promise.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he _____, and must be awaked.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.
Middle Test.note: Elijah's taunt on Mount Carmel: shout louder — maybe Baal is busy, travelling, or 'peradventure he sleepeth.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were _____.
Middle Test.verse: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
Middle Test.note: Paul paid his own way: he stayed with Aquila and Priscilla because they shared his trade — tentmaking.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury, and the form of his visage was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego: therefore he spake, and commanded that they should heat the furnace one _____ times more than it was wont to be heated.
Middle Test.verse: Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury, and the form of his visage was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego: therefore he spake, and commanded that they should heat the furnace one seven times more than it was wont to be heated.
Middle Test.note: Nebuchadnezzar was so furious he had the furnace heated seven times hotter — it made no difference.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a _____ gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
Middle Test.verse: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
Middle Test.note: Jesus pictures himself as a mother hen gathering her chicks — tender words for a city that kept refusing.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the ass saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his _____ drawn in his hand: and the ass turned aside out of the way, and went into the field: and Balaam smote the ass, to turn her into the way.
Middle Test.verse: And the ass saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand: and the ass turned aside out of the way, and went into the field: and Balaam smote the ass, to turn her into the way.
Middle Test.note: The donkey saw the angel with the drawn sword before the prophet did — and got beaten for being right.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when he had taken the book, the four beasts and four and twenty elders fell down before the Lamb, having every one of them _____, and golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints.
Middle Test.verse: And when he had taken the book, the four beasts and four and twenty elders fell down before the Lamb, having every one of them harps, and golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints.
Middle Test.note: Heaven's elders come with harps and golden vials full of odours — which turn out to be the prayers of saints.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But as one was felling a beam, the axe head fell into the water: and he cried, and said, Alas, master! for it was _____.
Middle Test.verse: But as one was felling a beam, the axe head fell into the water: and he cried, and said, Alas, master! for it was borrowed.
Middle Test.note: 'Alas, master! for it was borrowed' — the axe head sank, and the worker's real worry was paying it back.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among _____, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
Middle Test.verse: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
Middle Test.note: The Good Samaritan story begins on the Jericho road, with a man who fell among thieves and was left half dead.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So they poured out for the men to eat. And it came to pass, as they were eating of the pottage, that they cried out, and said, O thou man of God, there is _____ in the pot. And they could not eat thereof.
Middle Test.verse: So they poured out for the men to eat. And it came to pass, as they were eating of the pottage, that they cried out, and said, O thou man of God, there is death in the pot. And they could not eat thereof.
Middle Test.note: 'There is death in the pot!' — the prophets' stew was rescued when Elisha tossed in some meal.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of _____.
Middle Test.verse: And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.
Middle Test.note: One man wouldn't bow, and Haman was full of wrath — pride can't stand a single holdout.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a _____, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.
Middle Test.verse: And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.
Middle Test.note: Babel's builders wanted a tower reaching heaven and a name for themselves — God came down to see it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the _____ heaven.
Middle Test.verse: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.
Middle Test.note: Paul, modestly in the third person, describes a man caught up to the third heaven — and admits he can't say how.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the _____, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.
Middle Test.verse: And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.
Middle Test.note: From one rib, a whole woman — and Adam's first recorded words are a delighted 'bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And she said, As the LORD thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two _____, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.
Middle Test.verse: And she said, As the LORD thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.
Middle Test.note: The widow had a handful of meal, a little oil, and two sticks for one last meal — then Elijah asked for the first cake.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And suddenly there was a great _____, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.
Middle Test.verse: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.
Middle Test.note: At midnight in Philippi, an earthquake opened every prison door and loosed every prisoner's bands.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the house, when it was in building, was built of stone made ready before it was brought thither: so that there was neither _____ nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was in building.
Middle Test.verse: And the house, when it was in building, was built of stone made ready before it was brought thither: so that there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was in building.
Middle Test.note: The temple stones were cut off-site, so building it made no sound of hammer, axe, or iron tool.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But withal prepare me also a _____: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.
Middle Test.verse: But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.
Middle Test.note: Paul ends his note to Philemon hopeful of release: get a lodging ready for me.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that at the least the _____ of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them.
Middle Test.verse: Insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them.
Middle Test.note: The early church saw so many healings that people lined the streets hoping Peter's shadow would fall on them.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing _____ he went.
Middle Test.verse: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
Middle Test.note: Abraham obeyed and left home 'not knowing whither he went' — the first great road trip without a map.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he gave unto Moses, when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the _____ of God.
Middle Test.verse: And he gave unto Moses, when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God.
Middle Test.note: The Ten Commandments came 'written with the finger of God' — Jesus used the same phrase for casting out devils in Luke 11:20.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when Gideon was come, behold, there was a man that told a dream unto his fellow, and said, Behold, I dreamed a dream, and, lo, a cake of barley bread _____ into the host of Midian, and came unto a tent, and smote it that it fell, and overturned it, that the tent lay along.
Middle Test.verse: And when Gideon was come, behold, there was a man that told a dream unto his fellow, and said, Behold, I dreamed a dream, and, lo, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the host of Midian, and came unto a tent, and smote it that it fell, and overturned it, that the tent lay along.
Middle Test.note: A Midianite dreamed a barley loaf tumbled into camp and flattened a tent — Gideon overheard and worshipped.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of _____: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.
Middle Test.verse: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.
Middle Test.note: Paul's spiritual alarm clock: it's high time to awake out of sleep — salvation is nearer than when we believed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Moreover the king made a great throne of _____, and overlaid it with the best gold.
Middle Test.verse: Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the best gold.
Middle Test.note: Solomon's great throne was ivory overlaid with the best gold — six steps up, with twelve lions standing on them.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And being warned of God in a _____ that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.
Middle Test.verse: And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.
Middle Test.note: The wise men got their travel advisory in a dream and took another way home, skipping Herod entirely.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But the queen Vashti _____ to come at the king's commandment by his chamberlains: therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.
Middle Test.verse: But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment by his chamberlains: therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.
Middle Test.note: Queen Vashti refused to appear at the king's feast — and her empty seat opened the way for Esther.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he said unto them, Take me up, and _____ me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
Middle Test.verse: And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
Middle Test.note: Jonah's own solution to the storm: throw me overboard — and the sea will calm down.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being _____ is, God with us.
Middle Test.verse: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.
Middle Test.note: Matthew quotes Isaiah's prophecy and translates the name for his readers: Emmanuel means 'God with us.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then the angel of the LORD put forth the end of the _____ that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there rose up fire out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes. Then the angel of the LORD departed out of his sight.
Middle Test.verse: Then the angel of the LORD put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there rose up fire out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes. Then the angel of the LORD departed out of his sight.
Middle Test.note: The angel touched Gideon's offering with the tip of his staff, and fire leapt from the rock to consume it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small _____, whithersoever the governor listeth.
Middle Test.verse: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth.
Middle Test.note: Same lesson at sea: great ships driven by fierce winds still turn by a very small helm.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron's rod _____ up their rods.
Middle Test.verse: For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.
Middle Test.note: Pharaoh's magicians matched the trick, but Aaron's rod had the last word — it swallowed theirs whole.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her _____.
Middle Test.verse: So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging.
Middle Test.note: Over went Jonah, and the sea ceased from her raging — instantly.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he asked for a writing _____, and wrote, saying, His name is John. And they marvelled all.
Middle Test.verse: And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John. And they marvelled all.
Middle Test.note: Struck mute, Zacharias asked for a 'writing table' — a tablet — to settle his son's name once and for all: John.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of _____: and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
Middle Test.verse: And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
Middle Test.note: 'Receipt of custom' was the tax booth — Matthew was on the job collecting taxes when Jesus said, 'Follow me.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the _____? So run, that ye may obtain.
Middle Test.verse: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.
Middle Test.note: Paul borrows from the racetrack: everybody runs, but one gets the prize — so run like you mean it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the _____, and the seats of them that sold doves,
Middle Test.verse: And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,
Middle Test.note: Jesus overturned the moneychangers' tables in the temple — and the dove-sellers lost their seats too.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the _____ and harp.
Middle Test.verse: Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp.
Middle Test.note: The Bible's final psalm calls out the whole band — trumpet, psaltery, harp, and then everything that has breath.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And there shall come forth a _____ out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:
Middle Test.verse: And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots:
Middle Test.note: A rod from the stem of Jesse — a new shoot from David's family stump, long after the tree looked dead.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Now there is at Jerusalem by the sheep market a pool, which is called in the Hebrew tongue Bethesda, having five _____.
Middle Test.verse: Now there is at Jerusalem by the sheep market a pool, which is called in the Hebrew tongue Bethesda, having five porches.
Middle Test.note: The pool of Bethesda had five porches, crowded with the sick waiting for the moving of the water.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And _____ that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man's heart.
Middle Test.verse: And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man's heart.
Middle Test.note: Wine for gladness, oil for shining faces, bread for strength — the psalmist thanking God for a well-stocked table.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Also he sent forth a _____ from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground;
Middle Test.verse: Also he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground;
Middle Test.note: Noah's first scout was a raven that never reported back; the dove was the second try, and the one we remember.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's _____; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
Middle Test.verse: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
Middle Test.note: Jonah's own book says 'great fish,' but the KJV in Matthew says whale — and Jesus makes the three days a sign of his own.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves _____.
Middle Test.verse: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.
Middle Test.note: Fig-leaf aprons were Eden's first fashion line; the 1560 Geneva Bible said 'breeches,' earning it the nickname the Breeches Bible.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he said unto me, Son of man, cause thy belly to eat, and fill thy bowels with this roll that I give thee. Then did I eat it; and it was in my mouth as _____ for sweetness.
Middle Test.verse: And he said unto me, Son of man, cause thy belly to eat, and fill thy bowels with this roll that I give thee. Then did I eat it; and it was in my mouth as honey for sweetness.
Middle Test.note: Ezekiel was told to eat the scroll — and God's word tasted as sweet as honey.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Zadok the priest took an _____ of oil out of the tabernacle, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the trumpet; and all the people said, God save king Solomon.
Middle Test.verse: And Zadok the priest took an horn of oil out of the tabernacle, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the trumpet; and all the people said, God save king Solomon.
Middle Test.note: Zadok anointed Solomon from a horn of oil, the trumpet blew, and the people shouted, 'God save king Solomon.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Howbeit the hair of his head began to _____ again after he was shaven.
Middle Test.verse: Howbeit the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaven.
Middle Test.note: One quiet verse of hope: in the prison house, Samson's hair began to grow again.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And there appeared unto them _____ tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.
Middle Test.verse: And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.
Middle Test.note: 'Cloven' means split — the tongues like fire at Pentecost were divided, one settling on each of them.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one _____ in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
Middle Test.verse: For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
Middle Test.note: Matthew applies Isaiah's 'voice of one crying in the wilderness' to John the Baptist, the road crew for the coming King.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a _____, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone.
Middle Test.verse: So I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone.
Middle Test.note: Modern versions say rattling; the KJV says a noise and a shaking — and the dry bones came together, bone to his bone.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp _____ sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength.
Middle Test.verse: And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength.
Middle Test.note: In John's vision a sharp twoedged sword comes from Jesus' mouth — Hebrews 4:12 says the same of God's word.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two _____.
Middle Test.verse: And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.
Middle Test.note: Two mites made only a farthing (Mark 12:42), yet Jesus said this widow gave more than all the rich donors.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: The same hour was the thing fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and did eat _____ as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws.
Middle Test.verse: The same hour was the thing fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws.
Middle Test.note: Proud Nebuchadnezzar ate grass like an ox until he learned who really rules — then he praised the King of heaven.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our _____ are gone out.
Middle Test.verse: And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out.
Middle Test.note: The five foolish virgins brought lamps but no extra oil, and the wise ones wouldn't risk sharing theirs.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he looked, and, behold, there was a _____ baken on the coals, and a cruse of water at his head. And he did eat and drink, and laid him down again.
Middle Test.verse: And he looked, and, behold, there was a cake baken on the coals, and a cruse of water at his head. And he did eat and drink, and laid him down again.
Middle Test.note: An angel served the burned-out prophet a cake baked on hot coals and a jar of water — then let him nap again.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great _____ knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:
Middle Test.verse: And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:
Middle Test.note: Peter's rooftop vision: a great sheet let down by its four corners, full of creatures he'd never eat.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal _____ upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
Middle Test.verse: And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
Middle Test.note: The king set the royal crown on Esther's head — an orphan girl, now queen of Persia.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Behold the _____ of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
Middle Test.verse: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
Middle Test.note: The KJV's 'fowls of the air' are just birds — no barns, no savings plan, and fed every day anyway.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And had rained down manna upon them to eat, and had given them of the _____ of heaven.
Middle Test.verse: And had rained down manna upon them to eat, and had given them of the corn of heaven.
Middle Test.note: The psalmist calls manna 'the corn of heaven' — in KJV English, corn simply means grain.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things; a man plucked off his _____, and gave it to his neighbour: and this was a testimony in Israel.
Middle Test.verse: Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things; a man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour: and this was a testimony in Israel.
Middle Test.note: In old Israel a deal was sealed by handing over a shoe — the nearer kinsman's shoe gave Boaz the right to marry Ruth.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: That the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an _____ very far from the city Adam, that is beside Zaretan: and those that came down toward the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, failed, and were cut off: and the people passed over right against Jericho.
Middle Test.verse: That the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap very far from the city Adam, that is beside Zaretan: and those that came down toward the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, failed, and were cut off: and the people passed over right against Jericho.
Middle Test.note: When the priests' feet touched the Jordan, the river stood up in a heap far upstream — and Israel walked across.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Prove thy servants, I beseech thee, ten days; and let them give us _____ to eat, and water to drink.
Middle Test.verse: Prove thy servants, I beseech thee, ten days; and let them give us pulse to eat, and water to drink.
Middle Test.note: 'Pulse' means vegetables — Daniel's ten-day veggie challenge against the king's rich menu.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with _____.
Middle Test.verse: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
Middle Test.note: Rehoboam ignored the elders' advice and threatened scorpions instead of whips — and the kingdom split in two.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a _____, and poured oil upon the top of it.
Middle Test.verse: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.
Middle Test.note: After the ladder dream, Jacob turned his stone pillow into a pillar and anointed it — the place he named Beth-el.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For the king had at sea a navy of Tharshish with the navy of Hiram: once in three years came the navy of Tharshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and _____.
