Middle Test.verse: For the king had at sea a navy of Tharshish with the navy of Hiram: once in three years came the navy of Tharshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
Middle Test.note: Every three years Solomon's ships came home with gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks — a royal zoo shipment.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a _____ of the ground.
Middle Test.verse: And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
Middle Test.note: Abel kept sheep and Cain tilled the ground — the Bible's first two careers, and its first sibling rivalry right behind them.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Now Jacob's well was there. Jesus therefore, being _____ with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour.
Middle Test.verse: Now Jacob's well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour.
Middle Test.note: Even Jesus got tired: wearied from the journey, he sat on Jacob's well and soon met a Samaritan woman.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For thus saith the LORD God of Israel, The _____ of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth.
Middle Test.verse: For thus saith the LORD God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth.
Middle Test.note: God's promise to the widow: the barrel of meal won't run out and the oil won't fail until the rain comes.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: To him the _____ openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out.
Middle Test.verse: To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out.
Middle Test.note: The porter was the sheepfold's gatekeeper; the sheep follow because they know the shepherd's voice.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: As newborn babes, desire the sincere _____ of the word, that ye may grow thereby:
Middle Test.verse: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:
Middle Test.note: Peter's picture of spiritual growth: crave the word the way newborn babies crave milk.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild _____; and the angels ministered unto him.
Middle Test.verse: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.
Middle Test.note: Only Mark mentions that during the forty days of temptation Jesus was 'with the wild beasts.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with _____: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.
Middle Test.verse: And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.
Middle Test.note: Lazarus walked out still wrapped in graveclothes — Jesus' next instruction was simply, 'Loose him, and let him go.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an _____, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
Middle Test.note: Before he was a giant-slayer, David was Saul's personal musician, soothing the troubled king with his harp.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: To be taxed with Mary his _____ wife, being great with child.
Middle Test.verse: To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.
Middle Test.note: 'Espoused' means engaged — Mary and Joseph made the long trip to Bethlehem as a betrothed couple.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with _____?
Middle Test.verse: Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?
Middle Test.note: God's nature tour for Job includes the warhorse — its neck 'clothed with thunder,' where modern versions say mane.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's _____?
Middle Test.verse: And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?
Middle Test.note: After a three-day search, Jesus' first recorded words: he had to be about his Father's business.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the _____ of the ointment.
Middle Test.verse: Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment.
Middle Test.note: Mary of Bethany's pound of spikenard filled the whole house with its odour — a gift you could smell from every room.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Saul cast the _____; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it. And David avoided out of his presence twice.
Middle Test.verse: And Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it. And David avoided out of his presence twice.
Middle Test.note: Saul's jealousy took aim: he cast the javelin, and David sidestepped — twice.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of _____ was found upon him, because he believed in his God.
Middle Test.verse: Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.
Middle Test.note: Daniel came up from the den without a scratch, 'because he believed in his God.'

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And she went, and came, and gleaned in the field after the reapers: and her _____ was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.
Middle Test.verse: And she went, and came, and gleaned in the field after the reapers: and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.
Middle Test.note: 'Her hap was' — her luck was — to glean in a field belonging to Boaz; the book's quiet way of saying God arranged it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe _____, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.
Middle Test.verse: But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.
Middle Test.note: Nathan's parable of the poor man's one little ewe lamb — the story that trapped a king into judging himself.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his _____ and upward he was higher than any of the people.
Middle Test.verse: And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.
Middle Test.note: Saul looked the part: from his shoulders upward he was taller than anyone in Israel.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and said, Where is the LORD God of Elijah? and when he also had smitten the waters, they _____ hither and thither: and Elisha went over.
Middle Test.verse: And he took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and said, Where is the LORD God of Elijah? and when he also had smitten the waters, they parted hither and thither: and Elisha went over.
Middle Test.note: Elisha struck the Jordan with Elijah's fallen mantle, and the waters parted — the prophet's job had passed to him.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap _____ of fire on his head.
Middle Test.verse: Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.
Middle Test.note: Feeding your enemy 'heaps coals of fire on his head' — Paul quoting Proverbs 25:22, a kindness that burns.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in _____ with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
Middle Test.verse: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
Middle Test.note: Abraham lived in tents in the very land God had promised him — 'tabernacles' here simply means tents.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six _____; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.
Middle Test.verse: Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.
Middle Test.note: Each seraph had six wings: two to cover the face, two the feet, and two to fly — reverence takes most of them.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee _____ for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
Middle Test.verse: And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father's sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
Middle Test.note: For Jonathan's sake, David gave lame Mephibosheth his land back and a permanent seat at the king's table.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and _____ star.
Middle Test.verse: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.
Middle Test.note: Near the Bible's last page, Jesus names himself the root and offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then he returned, and walked in the house to and fro; and went up, and stretched himself upon him: and the child _____ seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
Middle Test.verse: Then he returned, and walked in the house to and fro; and went up, and stretched himself upon him: and the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
Middle Test.note: The Shunammite's son came back to life with seven sneezes — the only time 'sneezed' appears in the KJV.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Jesus saith unto him, Rise, take up thy _____, and walk.
Middle Test.verse: Jesus saith unto him, Rise, take up thy bed, and walk.
Middle Test.note: Thirty-eight years by the pool, then three commands from Jesus: rise, take up thy bed, and walk.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the LORD said unto Moses, Come up to me into the mount, and be there: and I will give thee _____ of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written; that thou mayest teach them.
Middle Test.verse: And the LORD said unto Moses, Come up to me into the mount, and be there: and I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written; that thou mayest teach them.
Middle Test.note: The KJV calls them 'tables of stone' — what most of us learned to call tablets.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he saw them toiling in _____; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.
Middle Test.verse: And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.
Middle Test.note: The disciples were toiling in rowing against a contrary wind when Jesus came by — walking on the sea.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the number of them that _____, putting their hand to their mouth, were three hundred men: but all the rest of the people bowed down upon their knees to drink water.
Middle Test.verse: And the number of them that lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, were three hundred men: but all the rest of the people bowed down upon their knees to drink water.
Middle Test.note: God's strange recruiting test: the three hundred who lapped water from their hands made Gideon's army.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And there arose a great _____ of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full.
Middle Test.verse: And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full.
Middle Test.note: A great storm of wind, a boat filling with water — and Jesus asleep in the back on a pillow.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when she knew Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for _____, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.
Middle Test.verse: And when she knew Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.
Middle Test.note: Rhoda was so glad to hear Peter's voice that she ran to tell everyone — and left him standing at the gate.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then said I, Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a _____.
Middle Test.verse: Then said I, Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.
Middle Test.note: Jeremiah's excuse when God called: 'I am a child' — God's answer was, don't say that, just go.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like _____ made with honey.
Middle Test.verse: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.
Middle Test.note: Manna's flavor review: white like coriander seed, tasting like wafers made with honey.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Nebuchadnezzar the king made an _____ of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.
Middle Test.verse: Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.
Middle Test.note: Nebuchadnezzar's golden image stood threescore cubits high — and everyone was ordered to bow.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they said one to another, Behold, this _____ cometh.
Middle Test.verse: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.
Middle Test.note: Joseph's brothers spotted him coming across the field and sneered, 'Behold, this dreamer cometh' — the dreams came true anyway.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And till Moses had done speaking with them, he put a _____ on his face.
Middle Test.verse: And till Moses had done speaking with them, he put a vail on his face.
Middle Test.note: The KJV spells it 'vail' — Moses' face shone so brightly after meeting God that he had to cover it.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a _____, and cried out:
Middle Test.verse: But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out:
Middle Test.note: Modern versions say 'ghost'; the KJV says the terrified disciples supposed Jesus walking on the sea was a spirit.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And thus shall ye eat it; with your _____ girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD'S passover.
Middle Test.verse: And thus shall ye eat it; with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD'S passover.
Middle Test.note: The first Passover was eaten dressed for travel: loins girded, shoes on, staff in hand — dinner with the bags packed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Ezra the scribe stood upon a _____ of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, and Shema, and Anaiah, and Urijah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, and Mishael, and Malchiah, and Hashum, and Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Middle Test.verse: And Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, and Shema, and Anaiah, and Urijah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, and Mishael, and Malchiah, and Hashum, and Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Middle Test.note: Ezra read the law from a 'pulpit of wood' — the only time the word pulpit appears in the KJV.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a _____ and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.
Middle Test.verse: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.
Middle Test.note: A sling and a stone — and the verse makes a point of it: no sword in David's hand.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And a _____ was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.
Middle Test.verse: And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.
Middle Test.note: A stone sealed with the king's own signet covered the lions' den — so no one could change the outcome.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there _____ the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
Middle Test.verse: Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
Middle Test.note: Babel's builders wanted to make a name; they got one — the place where the language got confounded.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal _____ of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.
Middle Test.verse: And Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a garment of fine linen and purple: and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.
Middle Test.note: Mordecai walked out in royal blue and white, with a great crown of gold — and the city of Shushan rejoiced.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a _____, and lighting upon him:
Middle Test.verse: And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:
Middle Test.note: At Jesus' baptism the heavens opened and the Spirit descended like a dove — Father, Son, and Spirit all in one scene.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the _____?
Middle Test.verse: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
Middle Test.note: Ten lepers healed, one came back to say thank you — and Jesus noticed the missing nine.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when they came unto the threshingfloor of Chidon, Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen _____.
Middle Test.verse: And when they came unto the threshingfloor of Chidon, Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled.
Middle Test.note: The oxen stumbled and Uzza reached out to steady the ark — a lesson that God's holy things are carried his way.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And let fall also some of the _____ of purpose for her, and leave them, that she may glean them, and rebuke her not.
Middle Test.verse: And let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and leave them, that she may glean them, and rebuke her not.
Middle Test.note: Boaz told his reapers to drop extra handfuls 'of purpose' for Ruth — kindness disguised as carelessness.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done many acts; he slew two lionlike men of Moab: also he went down and slew a lion in a pit in a _____ day.
Middle Test.verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done many acts; he slew two lionlike men of Moab: also he went down and slew a lion in a pit in a snowy day.
Middle Test.note: Benaiah's legendary résumé: he went down into a pit and slew a lion on a snowy day.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then she let them down by a _____ through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.
Middle Test.verse: Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.
Middle Test.note: Rahab's house was built into Jericho's wall, so the spies' escape route was simply a cord out her window.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For the king's ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram: every three years once came the ships of Tarshish bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and _____, and peacocks.
Middle Test.verse: For the king's ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram: every three years once came the ships of Tarshish bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
Middle Test.note: Solomon's ships brought home gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks — every three years, like clockwork.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For we are unto God a sweet _____ of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish:
Middle Test.verse: For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish:
Middle Test.note: Paul says believers are a 'sweet savour' of Christ to God — a fragrance that fills the room.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the LORD sent _____ serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.
Middle Test.verse: And the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.
Middle Test.note: Fiery serpents in the camp — the crisis that led to Moses lifting up the brass serpent on a pole.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, sat by the highway side _____.
Middle Test.verse: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, sat by the highway side begging.
Middle Test.note: Blind Bartimaeus sat begging by the Jericho roadside — and he was about to make a lot of noise.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass, that on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded _____.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass, that on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds.
Middle Test.note: Overnight, Aaron's dead walking stick budded, bloomed, and produced almonds — case closed on who God had chosen.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And in the _____ watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea.
Middle Test.verse: And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea.
Middle Test.note: The fourth watch was roughly 3 to 6 a.m. — the disciples had been out all night when Jesus came walking on the sea.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he looked up, and said, I see men as _____, walking.
Middle Test.verse: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.
Middle Test.note: A healing in two stages: after the first touch, the blind man of Bethsaida saw men like walking trees.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: So he departed thence, and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and he with the twelfth: and Elijah passed by him, and cast his _____ upon him.
Middle Test.verse: So he departed thence, and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and he with the twelfth: and Elijah passed by him, and cast his mantle upon him.
Middle Test.note: Elijah found Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and tossed his mantle over him — a job offer without words.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he said unto him, Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is _____ in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house.
Middle Test.verse: And he said unto him, Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house.
Middle Test.note: Gideon's objection: my family is poor and I'm the least in my father's house — just the kind of man God likes to use.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the _____ lay.
Middle Test.verse: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.
Middle Test.note: Friends dug through a roof to lower the man down — 'sick of the palsy' is the KJV's way of saying paralysed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered _____, a night and a day I have been in the deep;
Middle Test.verse: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;
Middle Test.note: Paul's résumé of hardships: thrice beaten with rods, once stoned, three shipwrecks, and a night and a day in the deep.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the LORD opened the _____ of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?
Middle Test.verse: And the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?
Middle Test.note: The Bible's only talking donkey — and her first words are a complaint about being hit three times.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the _____ of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them: and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
Middle Test.verse: Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them: and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.
Middle Test.note: A stone cut without hands smashed the great statue into chaff and grew into a mountain that filled the earth.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the _____, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.
Middle Test.verse: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.
Middle Test.note: Mary Magdalene's understandable mistake: through her tears she took the risen Jesus for the gardener.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick _____ in all the land of Egypt three days:
Middle Test.verse: And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days:
Middle Test.note: Three days of darkness so thick it could be felt — yet all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the _____ tree, I saw thee.
Middle Test.verse: Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.
Middle Test.note: Nathanael was stunned that Jesus had seen him under the fig tree before they had ever met.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the gates of it shall not be _____ at all by day: for there shall be no night there.
Middle Test.verse: And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there.
Middle Test.note: Ancient city gates were closed at night; heaven's gates are never shut, because there is no night there.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he commanded them to make all sit down by _____ upon the green grass.
Middle Test.verse: And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass.
Middle Test.note: Before feeding the five thousand, Jesus had everyone sit in companies on the green grass — crowd control, picnic style.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then I went down to the potter's house, and, behold, he wrought a work on the _____.
Middle Test.verse: Then I went down to the potter's house, and, behold, he wrought a work on the wheels.
Middle Test.note: Jeremiah's field trip to the potter's house, where the potter was hard at work on the wheels.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the princes, governors, and captains, and the king's counsellors, being gathered together, saw these men, upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head _____, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them.
Middle Test.verse: And the princes, governors, and captains, and the king's counsellors, being gathered together, saw these men, upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them.
Middle Test.note: Out of the furnace: not a hair singed, coats unchanged, not even the smell of smoke on them.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: The _____ that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.
Middle Test.verse: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.
Middle Test.note: Even apostles forget things: Paul asks Timothy to bring the cloke he left at Troas, plus the books and parchments.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a _____ of oil.
Middle Test.verse: And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.
Middle Test.note: Elisha asked the widow what she had in the house: just a pot of oil — which was all the miracle needed.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the _____ of heaven were opened.
Middle Test.verse: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.
Middle Test.note: Modern versions say floodgates; the KJV opens the 'windows of heaven' — the same phrase Malachi later uses for blessing.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And bring hither the _____ calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
Middle Test.verse: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
Middle Test.note: The fatted calf was saved for a big celebration — and the prodigal's homecoming was exactly that.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the _____ that remain, that nothing be lost.
Middle Test.verse: When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.
Middle Test.note: After feeding five thousand, Jesus still said not to waste the fragments — twelve baskets of leftovers.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a _____ by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.
Middle Test.verse: And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.
Middle Test.note: Caught by his horns in a thicket: the ram that took Isaac's place in the land of Moriah, right on time.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of _____ very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.
Middle Test.verse: And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.
Middle Test.note: Spikenard was a very precious ointment — and the woman broke the whole alabaster box and poured it on Jesus' head.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For Isaiah had said, Let them take a lump of _____, and lay it for a plaister upon the boil, and he shall recover.
Middle Test.verse: For Isaiah had said, Let them take a lump of figs, and lay it for a plaister upon the boil, and he shall recover.
Middle Test.note: Isaiah's prescription for King Hezekiah: a lump of figs laid on the boil — and the king recovered.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of _____, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.
Middle Test.verse: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.
Middle Test.note: Abigail's peace offering to David's hungry men: bread, wine, sheep, corn, raisins, and figs — she averted a disaster.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Thus saith the LORD unto me, Go and get thee a linen _____, and put it upon thy loins, and put it not in water.
Middle Test.verse: Thus saith the LORD unto me, Go and get thee a linen girdle, and put it upon thy loins, and put it not in water.
Middle Test.note: God's object lesson for Jeremiah: buy a linen girdle, wear it, then bury it by the river until it's ruined.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Therefore they enquired of the LORD further, if the man should yet come thither. And the LORD answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the _____.
Middle Test.verse: Therefore they enquired of the LORD further, if the man should yet come thither. And the LORD answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff.
Middle Test.note: Israel's first king, on coronation day, hid himself 'among the stuff' — the KJV's word for baggage.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, _____ souls were saved by water.
Middle Test.verse: Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.
Middle Test.note: Noah's ark carried just eight souls — Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their wives.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they came with _____, and found Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.
Middle Test.verse: And they came with haste, and found Mary, and Joseph, and the babe lying in a manger.
Middle Test.note: The shepherds didn't wait till morning — they came with haste and found the baby exactly as the angel said.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And there came an angel of the LORD, and sat under an oak which was in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abiezrite: and his son Gideon _____ wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites.
Middle Test.verse: And there came an angel of the LORD, and sat under an oak which was in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abiezrite: and his son Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites.
Middle Test.note: Gideon was threshing wheat down in a winepress to hide it — not exactly where you'd expect a mighty man of valour.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of _____:
Middle Test.verse: And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
Middle Test.note: Jesus nicknamed James and John 'sons of thunder' — the pair who later offered to call fire down from heaven (Luke 9:54).

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Balaam rose up in the morning, and _____ his ass, and went with the princes of Moab.
Middle Test.verse: And Balaam rose up in the morning, and saddled his ass, and went with the princes of Moab.
Middle Test.note: Balaam saddled his donkey and set out for Moab — about to be out-prophesied by the animal he was riding.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the _____ of Beth-lehem, which is by the gate!
Middle Test.verse: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Beth-lehem, which is by the gate!
Middle Test.note: David longed aloud for Bethlehem's well water; three mighty men fetched it — and he poured it out to the LORD.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the _____ were wrapped about my head.
Middle Test.verse: The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head.
Middle Test.note: From inside the fish Jonah prays about weeds wrapped around his head — the Bible's soggiest prayer.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were _____ about seven days.
Middle Test.verse: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they were compassed about seven days.
Middle Test.note: Jericho's walls fell after Israel compassed the city seven days — 'compassed' is KJV for marched around.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed _____ among the wheat, and went his way.
Middle Test.verse: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.
Middle Test.note: An enemy sowed tares among the wheat by night — and the farmer's advice was to let both grow until harvest.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty _____ sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold.
Middle Test.verse: And round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold.
Middle Test.note: Around heaven's throne sit 'four and twenty elders' in white raiment, wearing crowns of gold.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning _____, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.
Middle Test.verse: And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.
Middle Test.note: 'Cunning' here means skillful — Esau the outdoorsman, Jacob the homebody, and trouble brewing in the tents.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle's daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was _____ and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.
Middle Test.verse: And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle's daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was fair and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.
Middle Test.note: Esther, also called Hadassah, was an orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai as his own daughter.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a _____:
Middle Test.verse: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
Middle Test.note: The wise man's house stood because of what was under it — the rock is hearing Jesus' sayings and actually doing them.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil _____.
Middle Test.verse: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.
Middle Test.note: The oil kept pouring until every borrowed vessel was full — then it stayed, the moment the jars ran out.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for _____ pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
Middle Test.verse: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
Middle Test.note: Joseph's price: twenty pieces of silver, paid by traders headed for Egypt — where God was already a step ahead.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they came unto the brook of Eshcol, and cut down from thence a branch with one _____ of grapes, and they bare it between two upon a staff; and they brought of the pomegranates, and of the figs.
Middle Test.verse: And they came unto the brook of Eshcol, and cut down from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bare it between two upon a staff; and they brought of the pomegranates, and of the figs.
Middle Test.note: The spies' souvenir: one cluster of grapes so big it took two men and a staff to carry it home.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And they shall make an ark of _____ wood: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
Middle Test.verse: And they shall make an ark of shittim wood: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
Middle Test.note: The ark of the covenant was built of shittim wood — modern versions say acacia, a tough desert tree.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: Therefore Sarah _____ within herself, saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?
Middle Test.verse: Therefore Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?
Middle Test.note: Sarah laughed at the idea of a baby at her age; a year later she was laughing again, holding Isaac.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the _____, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.
Middle Test.verse: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.
Middle Test.note: Jesus' parable of the growing seed: blade, then ear, then full corn — the farmer sleeps and it grows anyway.

Middle Test.label: Sunday School
Middle Test.prompt: And Samson went and caught three hundred _____, and took firebrands, and turned tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the midst between two tails.
Middle Test.verse: And Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took firebrands, and turned tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the midst between two tails.
Middle Test.note: Three hundred foxes, paired tail to tail with torches — Samson's fiery revenge on the Philistines' grain fields.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in _____, fearful in praises, doing wonders?
Deep Water.verse: Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders?
Deep Water.note: The Song of the Sea: Israel's first worship chorus, sung on a beach still wet from the miracle.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: For the life of the flesh is in the _____: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.
Deep Water.verse: For the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.
Deep Water.note: Leviticus in one verse — why the altar exists, and why Hebrews keeps quoting it.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: God is not a man, that he should _____; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?
Deep Water.verse: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?
Deep Water.note: Balaam was hired to curse and could only bless: God doesn't take back his word — or need to.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: The _____ things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.
Deep Water.verse: The secret things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.
Deep Water.note: God keeps some files sealed; the revealed ones are plenty to keep us busy obeying.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the LORD was _____ from him.
Deep Water.verse: And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the LORD was departed from him.
Deep Water.note: The saddest 'wist not' in Scripture — Samson's strength left quietly, and he never felt it go.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are _____ than they that be with them.
Deep Water.verse: And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.
Deep Water.note: Elisha's servant saw an army; Elisha saw the mountain full of fiery chariots. Same hill, better eyesight.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my _____, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested.
Deep Water.verse: And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested.
Deep Water.note: The prayer of Jabez: 'coast' is KJV for territory — he asked God to move his fences outward.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: For the _____ of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.
Deep Water.verse: For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.
Deep Water.note: God isn't scanning for perfect people, but for hearts perfect toward him — Asa learned this the hard way.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Though he _____ me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.
Deep Water.verse: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.
Deep Water.note: Job's defiant trust: even the worst case doesn't cancel the contract.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Where wast thou when I laid the _____ of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
Deep Water.verse: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
Deep Water.note: God's opening question from the whirlwind — Job's résumé suddenly looked very short.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: As the _____ panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
Deep Water.verse: As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
Deep Water.note: A hart is a deer, not a 'heart' — though the psalmist means both kinds of thirst.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: So teach us to _____ our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
Deep Water.verse: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
Deep Water.note: Moses' math lesson: count your days honestly and wisdom starts adding up.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: They that sow in _____ shall reap in joy.
Deep Water.verse: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.
Deep Water.note: The exiles' harvest law: what you plant weeping, you carry home singing.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: A word fitly spoken is like _____ of gold in pictures of silver.
Deep Water.verse: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
Deep Water.note: The right word at the right moment is jewelry — 'pictures' here means settings of silver.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Where there is no _____, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
Deep Water.verse: Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
Deep Water.note: 'Vision' here is prophetic revelation — without a word from God, a people unravels.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Cast thy _____ upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
Deep Water.verse: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
Deep Water.note: The Preacher's case for generous risk: release it now, and it comes back with interest — eventually.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in _____ shall be your strength: and ye would not.
Deep Water.verse: For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not.
Deep Water.note: God's rescue plan was rest and quiet trust; Judah preferred fast horses. Note the ending: 'and ye would not.'

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy _____; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away.
Deep Water.verse: But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away.
Deep Water.note: Isaiah's brutal audit: even our best behavior, self-made, comes out of the wash filthy.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: The heart is _____ above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?
Deep Water.verse: The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?
Deep Water.note: Jeremiah's warning: the least trustworthy narrator you know lives in your own chest.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning _____ shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.
Deep Water.verse: Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.
Deep Water.note: Jeremiah tried to quit prophesying once — the word burned in his bones until he gave up giving up.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: It is good for a man that he bear the _____ in his youth.
Deep Water.verse: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.
Deep Water.note: The yoke is an ox harness, not an egg — Jeremiah says discipline learned young sits lighter.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the _____ before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none.
Deep Water.verse: And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none.
Deep Water.note: God went looking for one intercessor to stand in the breach — the vacancy went unfilled.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Again he said unto me, Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye _____ bones, hear the word of the LORD.
Deep Water.verse: Again he said unto me, Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.
Deep Water.note: Ezekiel preaches to a valley of skeletons — the least promising congregation in Scripture, and it revived.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not _____ thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
Deep Water.verse: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
Deep Water.note: The bravest 'but if not' ever spoken — the three friends trusted God's power without demanding the rescue.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And they that be _____ shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.
Deep Water.verse: And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.
Deep Water.note: Daniel's closing promise: soul-winners get stellar treatment — literally, shining like stars.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: My people are destroyed for lack of _____: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
Deep Water.verse: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me: seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
Deep Water.note: Hosea's diagnosis: Israel wasn't destroyed by armies but by ignorance they chose on purpose.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And I will restore to you the years that the _____ hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.
Deep Water.verse: And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.
Deep Water.note: God's promise after the plague: he can pay back years the swarm devoured — restoration with interest.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Can two walk together, except they be _____?
Deep Water.verse: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?
Deep Water.note: The first of Amos's rapid-fire questions — companionship runs on agreement, with God included.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord GOD, that I will send a _____ in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD:
Deep Water.verse: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord GOD, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD:
Deep Water.note: Amos's most haunting judgment: not empty stomachs, but silence from heaven.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Though thou exalt thyself as the _____, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the LORD.
Deep Water.verse: Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the LORD.
Deep Water.note: The shortest Old Testament book, aimed at Edom's cliff-top pride: no nest is above God's reach.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: They that observe lying _____ forsake their own mercy.
Deep Water.verse: They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.
Deep Water.note: Prayed from inside the fish: clinging to worthless idols means dropping the mercy already in your hands.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall _____; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me.
Deep Water.verse: Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me.
Deep Water.note: Micah's comeback verse: falling isn't final, and even his darkness has a light in it.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: The LORD is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the LORD hath his way in the _____ and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
Deep Water.verse: The LORD is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the LORD hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
Deep Water.note: Nahum to Nineveh: God's patience is not indifference — even the storm is his footpath.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: For the earth shall be filled with the _____ of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
Deep Water.verse: For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
Deep Water.note: Habakkuk's anchor amid Babylonian dread: God's glory will one day be as unavoidable as the ocean.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Seek ye the LORD, all ye _____ of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the LORD'S anger.
Deep Water.verse: Seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the LORD'S anger.
Deep Water.note: Zephaniah's survival advice for the day of the LORD: seek meekness, not higher ground.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: The _____ is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.
Deep Water.verse: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.
Deep Water.note: God's word to temple-builders worried about funding: the treasury was never the problem.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: For who hath despised the day of _____ things? for they shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel with those seven; they are the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth.
Deep Water.verse: For who hath despised the day of small things? for they shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel with those seven; they are the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth.
Deep Water.note: Zerubbabel's modest temple foundation looked like nothing — God says don't sneer at small starts.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with _____ in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.
Deep Water.verse: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.
Deep Water.note: The Old Testament's closing sunrise: for those who fear his name, healing comes with the dawn.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the _____ daily, whether those things were so.
Deep Water.verse: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
Deep Water.note: The Bereans got apostolic preaching and still checked the text daily — noble, says Luke.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Do all things without _____ and disputings:
Deep Water.verse: Do all things without murmurings and disputings:
Deep Water.note: Paul's shortest hard command — 'murmurings' is the grumble Israel perfected in the wilderness.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with _____, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.
Deep Water.verse: Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.
Deep Water.note: Paul's recipe for conversation: grace as the base, salt for savor — words that preserve, not sting.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: _____ all things; hold fast that which is good.
Deep Water.verse: Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.
Deep Water.note: 'Prove' means test, like assaying metal — examine everything, pocket only the good.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not _____, neither should he eat.
Deep Water.verse: For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.
Deep Water.note: Paul's blunt Thessalonian house rule — a correction for idlers, not for those who couldn't work.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Which hope we have as an _____ of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
Deep Water.verse: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
Deep Water.note: The only place Scripture calls hope an anchor — moored not to the seabed but inside the veil.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained _____ unawares.
Deep Water.verse: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
Deep Water.note: Abraham fed three strangers by his tent and got heaven's messengers — hospitality can outrank you.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a _____, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
Deep Water.verse: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
Deep Water.note: James's weather report on human life: morning mist, gone by breakfast — plan accordingly.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And beside this, giving all _____, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge;
Deep Water.verse: And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge;
Deep Water.note: Peter's growth ladder starts with effort: grace is free, but the climbing takes all diligence.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in _____ and in truth.
Deep Water.verse: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.
Deep Water.note: John's test of love: vocabulary is cheap; the proof ships in deeds and truth.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly _____ for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.
Deep Water.verse: Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.
Deep Water.note: Jude planned a pleasant letter and wrote a battle summons instead — the faith was worth the fight.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: So then because thou art _____, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.
Deep Water.verse: So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.
Deep Water.note: Laodicea's tepid water made the Lord gag — he'd rather have you hot or cold than room temperature.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my _____ come.
Deep Water.verse: If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.
Deep Water.note: Job asks the oldest question about death — and five chapters later answers it with 'I know that my redeemer liveth.'

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Thou therefore endure _____, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
Deep Water.verse: Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
Deep Water.note: KJV 'hardness' is hardship — Paul, chained in Rome, recruits Timothy as a fellow soldier.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Thus saith the LORD, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old _____, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.
Deep Water.verse: Thus saith the LORD, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.
Deep Water.note: God offers Judah the well-worn road to rest — and the verse ends with their blunt reply: 'We will not walk therein.'

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye _____ thee.
Deep Water.verse: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
Deep Water.note: Job's final confession: after all the debate, secondhand theology gave way to sight.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with _____, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil.
Deep Water.verse: And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil.
Deep Water.note: God combs Jerusalem by lamplight for the complacent — 'settled on their lees' is wine left too long on its dregs.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And _____ your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.
Deep Water.verse: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.
Deep Water.note: Tearing your robe was the classic grief gesture; Joel says God wants the heart torn instead — the clothes can stay.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for _____.
Deep Water.verse: And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.
Deep Water.note: Paul builds Romans 4 and Galatians 3 on this line — Abraham's faith was credited long before circumcision or the law.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Say unto them, As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I have no _____ in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?
Deep Water.verse: Say unto them, As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Israel?
Deep Water.note: God swears by his own life that he wants the wicked to turn and live — then pleads, 'turn ye, turn ye.'

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: For now we see through a glass, _____; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
Deep Water.verse: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
Deep Water.note: Corinth was famous for its bronze, mirrors included — Paul says our clearest view now is still a blurry reflection.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have _____, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.
Deep Water.verse: And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.
Deep Water.note: John cites this at the cross after the soldier's spear: 'They shall look on him whom they pierced.'

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the _____ his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil.
Deep Water.verse: Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil.
Deep Water.note: Jeremiah's proverb on habitual sin: some stains you can't scrub out yourself — hence the new-covenant promise later in his book.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: It is a _____ thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Deep Water.verse: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Deep Water.note: The sobering close to one of Hebrews' sternest warnings — the same hands that save are not to be trifled with.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a _____ people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
Deep Water.verse: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
Deep Water.note: 'Peculiar' here means God's own possession, not odd — though the world may struggle to tell the difference.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were _____ by the Holy Ghost.
Deep Water.verse: For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.
Deep Water.note: Peter's word for 'moved' is used of a ship borne along by the wind — the prophets sailed, the Spirit blew.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: But they shall sit every man under his _____ and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it.
Deep Water.verse: But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it.
Deep Water.note: Micah's peace picture — every family under its own vine and fig tree; George Washington loved quoting it in his letters.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of _____ was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name.
Deep Water.verse: Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name.
Deep Water.note: While cynics said serving God was pointless, the faithful kept talking — and heaven kept minutes.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the LORD, I will put my law in their _____ parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Deep Water.verse: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the LORD, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Deep Water.note: The new covenant: God's law moves from stone tablets to hearts — Hebrews 8 quotes the whole passage.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
Deep Water.prompt: And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered _____ fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not.
Deep Water.verse: And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not.
Deep Water.note: Aaron's sons improvised at the altar the day the priesthood began; the very next verse shows how seriously God took it.

Deep Water.label: Deep Water
