Pulpit Ready.verse: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Strait' means tight and narrow, as in straitjacket — not 'straight.' The KJV gate is cramped, not level.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For Ezra had _____ his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.
Pulpit Ready.note: Ezra's order of operations: seek, do, then teach — and first he 'prepared his heart.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Not forsaking the _____ of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
Pulpit Ready.note: Not forsaking 'the assembling of ourselves together' — the verse every pastor quotes about Sunday attendance.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For thus saith the high and lofty One that _____ eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.
Pulpit Ready.note: The God 'that inhabiteth eternity' also dwells with the contrite and humble — the highest address and the lowest.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the _____ of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
Pulpit Ready.verse: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
Pulpit Ready.note: A shout, the archangel's voice, and 'the trump of God' — the KJV keeps the old short form of trumpet.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
Pulpit Ready.note: Work it out with fear and 'trembling' — and the very next verse says it is God who works in you.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Hope _____ maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Hope deferred' — put off, postponed — and Proverbs admits it makes the heart sick. Honest wisdom.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with _____ living.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
Pulpit Ready.note: The prodigal 'wasted his substance with riotous living' — the KJV's elegant phrase for blowing it all.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For godly sorrow worketh _____ to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
Pulpit Ready.note: Godly sorrow 'worketh repentance'; worldly sorrow just works death. Paul's reminder that regret isn't repentance.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am _____; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts.
Pulpit Ready.note: Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up and cries 'I am undone' — unraveled first, then sent.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But one thing is _____: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
Pulpit Ready.note: Martha's kitchen, Mary's seat: 'one thing is needful.' Perhaps Jesus' gentlest correction.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: _____ the time, because the days are evil.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Redeeming the time' — buying up every opportunity, because the days are evil. Time management, Pauline edition.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not _____ for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.
Pulpit Ready.note: The passage that converted Augustine in a Milan garden in 386, after a voice said 'take up and read.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a _____ cord is not quickly broken.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'A threefold cord' — a wedding-sermon favorite, usually unpacked as husband, wife, and God.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that _____ closer than a brother.
Pulpit Ready.verse: A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'A friend that sticketh closer than a brother' — preachers have long heard Jesus in this one.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that _____ out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jesus answered Satan's first temptation with this verse: not bread only, but every word that 'proceedeth.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall _____ unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Pulpit Ready.note: To 'cleave' is to stick fast — the Bible's first wedding sermon, later quoted by both Jesus and Paul.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and _____ with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'A man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief' — the line Handel set in Messiah's aria 'He was despised.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
Pulpit Ready.note: Among the Old Testament verses most quoted in the New — Jesus used it to stump the Pharisees in Matthew 22.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the vessel that he made of clay was _____ in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the vessel that he made of clay was marred in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
Pulpit Ready.note: At the potter's house the vessel was 'marred,' so he made it again — the second-chance sermon in clay.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Bring ye all the tithes into the _____, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.
Pulpit Ready.note: God invites a test: bring the tithes into the 'storehouse,' then watch heaven's windows. Stewardship Sunday's anchor.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the LORD turned the _____ of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
Pulpit Ready.note: Job's turnaround came 'when he prayed for his friends' — the same friends who'd spent chapters lecturing him.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Looking unto Jesus the author and _____ of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jesus is 'the author and finisher' of faith — the one who starts it is the one who completes it.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the _____ are few;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;
Pulpit Ready.note: Plenteous harvest, few 'labourers' — the KJV keeps the British u. Missions Sunday in one sentence.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the _____, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
Pulpit Ready.note: Look back while plowing and the furrow goes crooked. The KJV spells it the British way: 'plough.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For we are his _____, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Workmanship' translates the Greek poiema — the root of our word 'poem.' You're God's handiwork.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against _____, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.
Pulpit Ready.note: The real fight isn't flesh and blood but 'principalities' and powers — spiritual-warfare sermons start here.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.
Pulpit Ready.note: The Psalter opens with a slow slide — walk, stand, sit — that ends in 'the seat of the scornful.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a _____ in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
Pulpit Ready.note: A psalm for the sons of Korah, whose clan really did keep the temple doors — and preferred it to wickedness's tents.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath _____ us into the kingdom of his dear Son:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son:
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Translated' means transferred — moved out of darkness's jurisdiction into the Son's kingdom, as Enoch was 'translated.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had _____ of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.
Pulpit Ready.note: The men of Issachar 'had understanding of the times' — every leadership sermon's favorite tribe.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For I _____ that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul runs the numbers — 'I reckon' — and present sufferings don't even compare to the glory ahead.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Kick against the pricks' — an ox kicking the farmer's goad, hurting only itself. Saul was the ox.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Preach the word; be _____ in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Be instant in season, out of season' — 'instant' meaning urgent and ready. An ordination-service favorite.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He must increase, but I must _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He must increase, but I must decrease.
Pulpit Ready.note: John the Baptist's whole job description in seven words: He must increase, but I must 'decrease.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou _____ me to be a Christian.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
Pulpit Ready.note: King Agrippa's near-miss — 'Almost thou persuadest me' — became P. P. Bliss's hymn 'Almost Persuaded.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a _____ cymbal.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.
Pulpit Ready.note: Gifts without love are just noise — 'sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.' The KJV calls love 'charity.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the _____ of the sea.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
Pulpit Ready.note: Sins cast into 'the depths of the sea' — Corrie ten Boom added that God then posts a sign: No Fishing Allowed.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son _____ us from all sin.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Cleanseth' is present tense in the Greek — it keeps on cleansing, not a one-time rinse.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his _____, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.
Pulpit Ready.note: Salt that has lost its 'savour' — KJV spelling, British u and all — is good for nothing but the road.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And it came to pass, when they were gone over, that Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double _____ of thy spirit be upon me.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And it came to pass, when they were gone over, that Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.
Pulpit Ready.note: Elisha asked for a 'double portion' — the firstborn son's inheritance share — of Elijah's spirit.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the _____ that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
Pulpit Ready.note: Saved 'to the uttermost' — completely, all the way through — because he 'ever liveth to make intercession.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, _____, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Stedfast, unmoveable' — two KJV spellings in a row that spellcheck would flag. Paul's charge after the resurrection chapter.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And they _____ him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'By the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony' — the classic testimony-service text.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Be sober, be _____; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Be sober, be vigilant' — written by Peter, who once fell asleep in Gethsemane when told to watch.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of _____; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.
Pulpit Ready.verse: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.
Pulpit Ready.note: Beauty for ashes, praise for 'heaviness' — from the very passage Jesus read aloud in the Nazareth synagogue.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, _____, and abundant in goodness and truth,
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth,
Pulpit Ready.note: God's own self-description to Moses on Sinai — 'longsuffering,' the KJV's one word for slow to anger.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel? how shall I make thee as Admah? how shall I set thee as Zeboim? mine heart is turned within me, my _____ are kindled together.
Pulpit Ready.verse: How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel? how shall I make thee as Admah? how shall I set thee as Zeboim? mine heart is turned within me, my repentings are kindled together.
Pulpit Ready.note: God's heart turns within him over Ephraim — 'my repentings are kindled together.' Love wrestling with justice.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The LORD will perfect that which _____ me: thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me: thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me' — he finishes what he starts, Philippians 1:6 in psalm form.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Ye shall keep my sabbaths, and _____ my sanctuary: I am the LORD.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Ye shall keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary: I am the LORD.
Pulpit Ready.note: Keep my sabbaths, 'reverence' my sanctuary — holy time and holy space, repeated word for word in Leviticus 26:2.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not _____ unto the heavenly vision:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul before King Agrippa, summing up the Damascus road: 'I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him _____, smitten of God, and afflicted.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.
Pulpit Ready.note: He carried our griefs, yet we thought him 'stricken, smitten of God' — the great misreading of the Servant's suffering.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Rest in the LORD, and wait _____ for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him' — Psalm 37 says 'fret not thyself' three times (verses 1, 7, and 8).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and _____ as doves.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jesus' briefing before sending out the Twelve: wise as serpents, and 'harmless' as doves — innocent of any guile.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation: and thy _____ hath made me great.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation: and thy gentleness hath made me great.
Pulpit Ready.note: David's victory song credits God's strength, not his own: 'thy gentleness hath made me great' — sung again in Psalm 18:35.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a _____ of them openly, triumphing over them in it.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Shew' is the KJV's spelling of show: Christ made a public spectacle of the powers he disarmed at the cross.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The wind bloweth where it _____, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'The wind bloweth where it listeth' — where it pleases. Jesus to Nicodemus, by night, on being born of the Spirit.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the _____ shall be made straight, and the rough places plain:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain:
Pulpit Ready.note: Valleys raised, mountains lowered, 'the crooked shall be made straight' — road crews clearing the way for the coming King.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: What shall I _____ unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me?
Pulpit Ready.verse: What shall I render unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me?
Pulpit Ready.note: The grateful psalmist asks what he can 'render' for all God's benefits. His answer (v. 13): take the cup of salvation.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto _____ much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.
Pulpit Ready.note: The stewardship principle in a sentence: 'unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he was afraid, and said, How _____ is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jacob woke from the ladder dream: 'How dreadful is this place!' — dread as holy awe at the very gate of heaven.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Neither filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor _____, which are not convenient: but rather giving of thanks.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Neither filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting, which are not convenient: but rather giving of thanks.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's list of what's 'not convenient' — not fitting — for saints ends with an upgrade: giving of thanks.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are _____, but not in despair;
Pulpit Ready.verse: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair;
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's paradox list: troubled but not distressed, 'perplexed' but not in despair.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the _____ of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive;
Pulpit Ready.verse: That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive;
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Sleight' as in sleight of hand — trickery, not 'slight.' Paul warns against doctrine dealt by card sharps.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: It is the spirit that _____; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.
Pulpit Ready.verse: It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Quickeneth' means gives life. Moments later Peter answers: 'thou hast the words of eternal life' (verse 68).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I the LORD search the heart, I try the _____, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.
Pulpit Ready.verse: I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.
Pulpit Ready.note: God searches the heart and tries the 'reins' — the old English word for kidneys, pictured as the seat of hidden motives.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: His glory is like the firstling of his bullock, and his horns are like the horns of _____: with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.
Pulpit Ready.verse: His glory is like the firstling of his bullock, and his horns are like the horns of unicorns: with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.
Pulpit Ready.note: Yes, the KJV has 'unicorns' — Moses' blessing on Joseph's mighty horns. Most modern versions say 'wild ox.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath _____ upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Behold, what manner of love' — John pauses mid-letter to marvel that we're called the sons of God.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the _____ from on high hath visited us,
Pulpit Ready.verse: Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us,
Pulpit Ready.note: Zacharias' song over newborn John: the 'dayspring from on high' — the sunrise — has visited us.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Charity never _____: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Charity never faileth' — prophecies, tongues, and knowledge all have an expiry date; love doesn't.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which _____ not.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'The law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not' — the legal trap that sent Daniel to the lions' den.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And her prophets have daubed them with _____ morter, seeing vanity, and divining lies unto them, saying, Thus saith the Lord GOD, when the LORD hath not spoken.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And her prophets have daubed them with untempered morter, seeing vanity, and divining lies unto them, saying, Thus saith the Lord GOD, when the LORD hath not spoken.
Pulpit Ready.note: False prophets 'daubed' a crumbling wall with 'untempered morter' — whitewash that won't hold. Yes, the KJV spells it morter.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but _____ to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Condescend to men of low estate' — in KJV English a good thing: stoop gladly to fellowship with the lowly.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having _____ ears;
Pulpit Ready.verse: For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Itching ears' — audiences who shop for teachers that scratch where it itches. Paul's forecast for Timothy.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Beware lest any man spoil you through _____ and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's warning to Colossae: don't let anyone 'spoil' you — carry you off as plunder — through hollow philosophy.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no _____ of persons:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
Pulpit Ready.note: Peter in Cornelius's house, learning his rooftop vision's lesson: God is no 'respecter' of persons — no favorites.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Now therefore fear the LORD, and serve him in _____ and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the LORD.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Now therefore fear the LORD, and serve him in sincerity and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the LORD.
Pulpit Ready.note: Joshua's farewell: serve the LORD 'in sincerity and in truth' — the next verse is his famous 'as for me and my house.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The fire shall ever be _____ upon the altar; it shall never go out.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The fire shall ever be burning upon the altar; it shall never go out.
Pulpit Ready.note: The altar fire was never to go out — it 'shall ever be burning' — a favorite picture of devotion that never cools.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his _____, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Subtilty' is the KJV's spelling of subtlety — the serpent's cunning that beguiled Eve in the garden.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: O Lord, I beseech thee, let now thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant, and to the prayer of thy servants, who desire to fear thy name: and prosper, I pray thee, thy servant this day, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man. For I was the king's _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: O Lord, I beseech thee, let now thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant, and to the prayer of thy servants, who desire to fear thy name: and prosper, I pray thee, thy servant this day, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man. For I was the king's cupbearer.
Pulpit Ready.note: Nehemiah's prayer ends with his job title: 'For I was the king's cupbearer' — trusted access he was about to use.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And whosoever shall _____ thee to go a mile, go with him twain.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.
Pulpit Ready.note: Going the second mile starts here: compelled to go one mile? Go with him 'twain' — that's two.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a _____ savour.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.
Pulpit Ready.note: Christ's self-giving as 'a sweetsmelling savour' — offering language straight out of Leviticus, in one KJV compound.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But your iniquities have _____ between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.
Pulpit Ready.note: God's arm isn't short nor his ear heavy (59:1); the problem is that 'your iniquities have separated' you from him.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Wherefore the LORD God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Wherefore the LORD God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.
Pulpit Ready.note: Spoken against Eli's house — and slipped to Eric Liddell in a note before his 1924 Olympic 400m final, which he won.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: A good name is better than _____ ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
Pulpit Ready.verse: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
Pulpit Ready.note: A good name beats 'precious ointment' — and in Hebrew the two words even sound alike: shem and shemen.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: To the Lord our God belong mercies and _____, though we have rebelled against him;
Pulpit Ready.verse: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against him;
Pulpit Ready.note: Daniel's great prayer: we rebelled, yet to God belong 'mercies and forgivenesses' — plural, because one would never be enough.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And without _____ great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Without controversy' — no argument here — great is the mystery of godliness, summed up in six crisp lines about Christ.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the _____' den.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice' den.
Pulpit Ready.note: In the peaceable kingdom a weaned child reaches into the 'cockatrice' den — the KJV's name for a deadly serpent.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and _____ evil?
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?
Pulpit Ready.note: God's own résumé for Job: perfect, upright, fearing God, and one that 'escheweth evil' — turns his back on it.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the times of this ignorance God _____ at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
Pulpit Ready.note: 'God winked at' past ignorance — overlooked it — but now commands all men everywhere to repent.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will _____ purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
Pulpit Ready.note: Not a typo: 'throughly' is the KJV's old form of thoroughly. John the Baptist's winnowing fan leaves nothing unsifted.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable.
Pulpit Ready.note: Psalm 145, titled 'David's Psalm of praise,' calls God's greatness 'unsearchable' — a well with no bottom.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: There _____ therefore a rest to the people of God.
Pulpit Ready.verse: There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'There remaineth therefore a rest' — a Sabbath-rest for God's people that the land of Canaan only previewed.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For I am _____, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
Pulpit Ready.verse: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
Pulpit Ready.note: The start of Paul's great list — death, life, angels, powers — that climaxes in verse 39: nothing can separate us.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all _____ and supplication for all saints;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints;
Pulpit Ready.note: The armour of God passage ends not with a weapon but with prayer — watching 'with all perseverance.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Let nothing be done through strife or _____; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Vainglory' is empty glory, conceit. Paul's cure: lowliness of mind, each esteeming others better than himself.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he shall restore the lamb _____, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
Pulpit Ready.note: David judged Nathan's story of the stolen lamb: restore it 'fourfold.' Nathan's reply: 'Thou art the man.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath _____ gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
Pulpit Ready.note: Miriam, timbrel in hand, led Israel's women in the victory song at the sea: he 'hath triumphed gloriously.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Lord, now _____ thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word:
Pulpit Ready.note: Old Simeon, holding the baby Jesus in the temple: now 'lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, _____ is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul quotes Deuteronomy 32:35 — 'Vengeance is mine' — as the reason to leave payback in God's hands.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the LORD, and the other lot for the _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the LORD, and the other lot for the scapegoat.
Pulpit Ready.note: On the day of atonement one goat was offered, and the other, the 'scapegoat,' carried Israel's sins into the wilderness.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: My son, despise not the _____ of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction:
Pulpit Ready.verse: My son, despise not the chastening of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction:
Pulpit Ready.note: Don't despise the LORD's 'chastening' — Hebrews 12:5–6 quotes this to show that discipline is proof of sonship.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy _____ delight my soul.
Pulpit Ready.verse: In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul.
Pulpit Ready.note: When anxious thoughts multiply, God's 'comforts' delight the soul — the KJV's answer to a racing mind at 3 a.m.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And while he _____, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the LORD being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the LORD being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.
Pulpit Ready.note: Even with judgment at the door, Lot 'lingered' — so the angels took him by the hand, 'the LORD being merciful unto him.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: So we fasted and _____ our God for this: and he was intreated of us.
Pulpit Ready.verse: So we fasted and besought our God for this: and he was intreated of us.
Pulpit Ready.note: Ezra was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers (8:22), so the people fasted and 'besought' God instead — and he listened.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a _____ of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by:
Pulpit Ready.verse: And it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by:
Pulpit Ready.note: Moses was tucked into 'a clift of the rock' while God's glory passed by — the KJV's old spelling of cleft.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.
Pulpit Ready.note: After losing everything in one day, Job worshipped: 'In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: She hath done what she could: she is come _____ to anoint my body to the burying.
Pulpit Ready.verse: She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying.
Pulpit Ready.note: Defending the woman with the costly ointment at Bethany: she anointed his body 'aforehand' for burial.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But there is a God in heaven that _____ secrets, and maketh known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Thy dream, and the visions of thy head upon thy bed, are these;
Pulpit Ready.verse: But there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets, and maketh known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Thy dream, and the visions of thy head upon thy bed, are these;
Pulpit Ready.note: Before Nebuchadnezzar, Daniel took no credit at all: 'there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was much _____ because of the way.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way.
Pulpit Ready.note: The long detour around Edom wore Israel down — 'much discouraged because of the way' — and the fiery serpents followed.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Righteousness _____ a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people.
Pulpit Ready.note: A civics lecture in one line: righteousness 'exalteth' a nation, but sin is a reproach to any people.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
Pulpit Ready.note: Blind eyes opened, deaf ears 'unstopped' — Jesus pointed John the Baptist's disciples to exactly these signs (Matthew 11:5).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: _____ silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jeremiah's refining image ends grimly: silver that won't purify is 'reprobate silver,' because the LORD hath rejected it.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, _____ thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes;
Pulpit Ready.note: Enlarge the tent, 'lengthen thy cords' — the text of William Carey's 1792 'Expect great things' missions sermon.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: All things are lawful for me, but all things are not _____: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not.
Pulpit Ready.verse: All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'All things are lawful… but not expedient' — Paul's two-part test: is it allowed, and is it actually helpful?

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them, and _____ the word with signs following. Amen.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following. Amen.
Pulpit Ready.note: Mark's Gospel closes with the apostles preaching everywhere and the Lord 'confirming the word with signs following.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are _____ wolves.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.
Pulpit Ready.note: False prophets in sheep's clothing, 'inwardly ravening wolves' — the original wolf in sheep's clothing.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and _____ sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.
Pulpit Ready.verse: From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.
Pulpit Ready.note: Isaiah's diagnosis of a sinful nation: wounds, bruises, and 'putrifying sores' — note the KJV spelling — with no one to bind them.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is _____ to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
Pulpit Ready.note: Why the delay? God is not 'slack' — he's 'longsuffering,' not willing that any should perish.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The officers answered, Never man _____ like this man.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The officers answered, Never man spake like this man.
Pulpit Ready.note: Temple officers sent to arrest Jesus came back empty-handed with this excuse: 'Never man spake like this man.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the king said, Enquire thou whose son the _____ is.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the king said, Enquire thou whose son the stripling is.
Pulpit Ready.note: After Goliath fell, Saul asked whose son 'the stripling' was — a lad barely grown, suddenly Israel's hero.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For whom the Lord loveth he _____, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
Pulpit Ready.note: Hebrews quotes Proverbs 3:12: whom the Lord loveth he 'chasteneth' — discipline as proof you're a true son.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he shall be thy _____ unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.
Pulpit Ready.note: God's compromise for a reluctant Moses: Aaron would be his 'spokesman' — the only time the KJV uses the word.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one _____ shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'One jot or one tittle' — the smallest Hebrew letter and the tiniest pen-stroke. Not one will pass from the Law.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast' — a shelter-in-place word for storms.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye _____ ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of the LORD your God which I command you.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of the LORD your God which I command you.
Pulpit Ready.note: Don't add, don't 'diminish' — Moses' rule for God's word, echoed in the Bible's closing warning (Revelation 22:18–19).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask _____, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.
Pulpit Ready.note: Unanswered prayer, diagnosed: ye ask 'amiss' — wrongly — to spend it on your own lusts.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: As the _____ sitteth on eggs, and hatcheth them not; so he that getteth riches, and not by right, shall leave them in the midst of his days, and at his end shall be a fool.
Pulpit Ready.verse: As the partridge sitteth on eggs, and hatcheth them not; so he that getteth riches, and not by right, shall leave them in the midst of his days, and at his end shall be a fool.
Pulpit Ready.note: Ill-gotten riches are like a 'partridge' sitting on eggs that never hatch — 'at his end' such a man 'shall be a fool.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he _____ the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding:
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding:
Pulpit Ready.note: Daniel's praise after the dream was revealed: God 'changeth the times and the seasons' and removes and sets up kings.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Wherefore let him that thinketh he _____ take heed lest he fall.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.
Pulpit Ready.note: Right after recounting Israel's wilderness failures: 'let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The _____ of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.
Pulpit Ready.note: Keep the true fast and you shall be called 'The repairer of the breach' — a rebuilder of broken walls and paths.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy _____ out of his place, except thou repent.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.
Pulpit Ready.note: To Ephesus, who had left their first love: repent, or I will 'remove thy candlestick' — the church's lamp.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one _____ in one place.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.
Pulpit Ready.note: When the day of Pentecost 'was fully come,' the disciples were all together 'with one accord' — of one mind.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And have no fellowship with the _____ works of darkness, but rather reprove them.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them.
Pulpit Ready.note: Darkness produces nothing worth keeping: its works are 'unfruitful' — so don't join in; expose them.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah _____ and fire from the LORD out of heaven;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;
Pulpit Ready.note: Fire and 'brimstone' on Sodom and Gomorrah — the scene behind Jesus' shortest warning: 'Remember Lot's wife' (Luke 17:32).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Many shall be _____, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.
Pulpit Ready.note: In the end 'many shall be purified, and made white, and tried' — and only the wise shall understand.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: _____ themselves to be wise, they became fools,
Pulpit Ready.verse: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
Pulpit Ready.note: The great irony in eight words: 'Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof is _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof is brutish.
Pulpit Ready.note: Proverbs doesn't soften it: love instruction and you love knowledge; hate reproof and you're 'brutish.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
Pulpit Ready.note: Written in bonds (1:13): Paul says he 'learned' to be content — it didn't come naturally even to him.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And David _____ all that the Amalekites had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.
Pulpit Ready.note: At Ziklag David lost everything; after he 'encouraged himself in the LORD' (30:6), he 'recovered all.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He, that being often reproved _____ his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
Pulpit Ready.note: Reproved often but still 'hardeneth his neck' — he 'shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.' Warnings run out.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was _____, and rose up in haste, and spake, and said unto his counsellors, Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? They answered and said unto the king, True, O king.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied, and rose up in haste, and spake, and said unto his counsellors, Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? They answered and said unto the king, True, O king.
Pulpit Ready.note: Nebuchadnezzar was 'astonied' — the KJV's old form of astonished — on seeing a fourth man walking in the fire.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He that _____ a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.
Pulpit Ready.note: Answering a matter before you've heard it is 'folly and shame' — the ancient rule against interrupting.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Doth not behave itself _____, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;
Pulpit Ready.note: Love's etiquette: it 'doth not behave itself unseemly' — no rudeness — and it is not easily provoked.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For our light _____, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;
Pulpit Ready.verse: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's scales: a 'light affliction' for a moment versus 'an eternal weight of glory' — no contest.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a _____ place, and there prayed.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
Pulpit Ready.note: After a long evening of healing in Capernaum, Jesus rose 'a great while before day' to pray alone.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Blessed is he whose _____ is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
Pulpit Ready.note: David's song of forgiveness opens with a blessing on the one whose 'transgression' is forgiven. Paul quotes it in Romans 4:7.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the _____ of sin for a season;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
Pulpit Ready.note: Moses chose suffering with God's people over 'the pleasures of sin for a season' — enjoyable, but temporary.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this _____ of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?
Pulpit Ready.verse: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?
Pulpit Ready.note: Saul claimed full obedience; Samuel heard sheep. 'What meaneth then this bleating?' — caught out by livestock.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But Martha was _____ about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.
Pulpit Ready.note: Martha 'was cumbered about much serving' — weighed down by the busywork — while Mary sat at Jesus' feet.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious _____ of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;
Pulpit Ready.note: 'That blessed hope, and the glorious appearing' — the Second Coming, as Paul framed it for Titus on Crete.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Thou hast made us as the _____ and refuse in the midst of the people.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jerusalem made 'the offscouring and refuse' among nations — Paul uses the same word for the apostles in 1 Corinthians 4:13.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Now unto him that is able to do _____ abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,
Pulpit Ready.verse: Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,
Pulpit Ready.note: The doxology that outruns imagination: 'exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him _____ that taketh his name in vain.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
Pulpit Ready.note: The third commandment carries a warning label: the LORD will not hold him 'guiltless' who takes his name in vain.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And they come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people, and they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And they come unto thee as the people cometh, and they sit before thee as my people, and they hear thy words, but they will not do them: for with their mouth they shew much love, but their heart goeth after their covetousness.
Pulpit Ready.note: Ezekiel's hearers enjoyed him like a lovely song (33:32) — but their hearts went after 'covetousness.' Hearers, not doers.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And I will rebuke the _____ for your sakes, and he shall not destroy the fruits of your ground; neither shall your vine cast her fruit before the time in the field, saith the LORD of hosts.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, and he shall not destroy the fruits of your ground; neither shall your vine cast her fruit before the time in the field, saith the LORD of hosts.
Pulpit Ready.note: Bring the tithes, and God will 'rebuke the devourer' — no more crops lost before harvest. The promise right after the storehouse.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it _____ me nothing.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.
Pulpit Ready.note: Even giving everything away, even martyrdom, without love adds up to zero: 'it profiteth me nothing.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But when ye pray, use not vain _____, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jesus' warning just before the Lord's Prayer: God isn't impressed by 'vain repetitions' or word count.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He that hath pity upon the poor _____ unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
Pulpit Ready.note: Give to the poor and you're making a loan to the LORD — and Proverbs promises he will pay it back.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: That by two _____ things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
Pulpit Ready.verse: That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
Pulpit Ready.note: God's promise plus his oath: 'two immutable things' — unchangeable — anchoring the hope set before us.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: It is better to dwell in a corner of the _____, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.
Pulpit Ready.verse: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.
Pulpit Ready.note: Better a corner of the 'housetop' than a wide house with a brawling woman — Proverbs liked it enough to say it twice (25:24).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Thy _____ waxed not old upon thee, neither did thy foot swell, these forty years.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Thy raiment waxed not old upon thee, neither did thy foot swell, these forty years.
Pulpit Ready.note: Forty years in the desert and their 'raiment waxed not old' — no worn-out clothes, no swollen feet. Wilderness miracles.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The fear of man bringeth a _____: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.
Pulpit Ready.note: People-pleasing is a trap: 'the fear of man bringeth a snare' — but whoso trusts the LORD shall be safe.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire _____!
Pulpit Ready.verse: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!
Pulpit Ready.note: James on the tongue: a tiny member, a big boast — 'how great a matter a little fire kindleth!'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the watchman told, saying, He came even unto them, and cometh not again: and the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi; for he driveth _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the watchman told, saying, He came even unto them, and cometh not again: and the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi; for he driveth furiously.
Pulpit Ready.note: The watchman recognized Jehu by his driving: 'he driveth furiously' — Scripture's most famous chariot speeder.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that _____ in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:
Pulpit Ready.verse: We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:
Pulpit Ready.note: Scripture as a lamp that 'shineth in a dark place' until the day dawns and the day star rises in your heart.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The _____ of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.
Pulpit Ready.note: Not the whole Bible at once — just 'the entrance of thy words giveth light.' Open the door a crack and light floods in.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But we all, with open face beholding as in a _____ the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.
Pulpit Ready.note: In the KJV a 'glass' is a mirror — beholding the Lord's glory, we're changed 'from glory to glory.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: No man that warreth _____ himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.
Pulpit Ready.verse: No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.
Pulpit Ready.note: No soldier on duty 'entangleth himself' with civilian affairs — he aims to please the one who enlisted him.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not _____ thy son, thine only son from me.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.
