Pulpit Ready.note: At Moriah the knife was stopped: Abraham had not 'withheld' his only son — echoed in Romans 8:32's 'spared not his own Son.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to _____ all the fiery darts of the wicked.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.
Pulpit Ready.note: The shield of faith can 'quench all the fiery darts of the wicked' — flaming arrows put out on impact.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her _____ is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.
Pulpit Ready.note: Silent as a sheep before her 'shearers' — the Ethiopian eunuch was reading this very passage when Philip arrived (Acts 8:32).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Behold now _____, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.
Pulpit Ready.note: God points Job to 'behemoth,' a grass-eating giant: 'he is the chief of the ways of God' (40:19).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the vine said unto them, Should I leave my wine, which _____ God and man, and go to be promoted over the trees?
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the vine said unto them, Should I leave my wine, which cheereth God and man, and go to be promoted over the trees?
Pulpit Ready.note: In Jotham's fable the vine refuses to be king of the trees: why leave my wine, 'which cheereth God and man'?

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Moreover it is required in _____, that a man be found faithful.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.
Pulpit Ready.note: The one qualification Paul lists for stewards: not talent, not charisma — just being found faithful.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the LORD said, My spirit shall not always _____ with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the LORD said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.
Pulpit Ready.note: Before the flood, God set a limit: 'My spirit shall not always strive with man' — his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: There the wicked cease from _____; and there the weary be at rest.
Pulpit Ready.verse: There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest.
Pulpit Ready.note: Job, wishing he'd never been born, pictures the grave as rest: there the wicked cease from 'troubling,' and the weary rest.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The grass _____, the flower fadeth: because the spirit of the LORD bloweth upon it: surely the people is grass.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: because the spirit of the LORD bloweth upon it: surely the people is grass.
Pulpit Ready.note: The grass 'withereth,' the flower fadeth — but the very next verse says the word of our God shall stand for ever.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the LORD said unto Moses, Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go _____:
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the LORD said unto Moses, Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward:
Pulpit Ready.note: At the Red Sea, God told Moses to stop crying out and start marching: speak unto Israel, 'that they go forward.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for those: the _____ men, though fools, shall not err therein.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for those: the wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein.
Pulpit Ready.note: The way of holiness is so plain that 'wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein.' A highway even we can't miss.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not _____ come out of your mouth: for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
Pulpit Ready.note: Hannah's song warns the proud: let not 'arrogancy' come out of your mouth — the KJV's longer cousin of arrogance.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For God is not the author of _____, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints.
Pulpit Ready.note: God is not 'the author of confusion' — Paul's case for orderly worship in a very noisy Corinth.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour _____ one another;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another;
Pulpit Ready.note: 'In honour preferring one another' — Paul's idea of competition: outdo each other in showing respect.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: That which the _____ hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm hath left hath the caterpiller eaten.
Pulpit Ready.verse: That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm hath left hath the caterpiller eaten.
Pulpit Ready.note: Joel's plague comes in four waves — palmerworm, locust, cankerworm, caterpiller — and the KJV spells that last one oddly too.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For he _____ the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.
Pulpit Ready.note: God 'satisfieth the longing soul' — then Psalm 107 tells rescue stories of wanderers, prisoners, the sick, and storm-tossed sailors.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the manna was as _____ seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the manna was as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium.
Pulpit Ready.note: Manna looked like 'coriander' seed and tasted like wafers made with honey (Exodus 16:31) — and Israel still complained.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the _____ of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's shorter armour list: the 'breastplate of faith and love,' and the hope of salvation for a helmet.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Use hospitality one to another without _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Use hospitality one to another without grudging.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Use hospitality one to another without grudging' — open the door, and keep the complaints to yourself.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And my people are bent to _____ from me: though they called them to the most High, none at all would exalt him.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And my people are bent to backsliding from me: though they called them to the most High, none at all would exalt him.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'My people are bent to backsliding from me' — and in the very next verse God cries, 'How shall I give thee up?'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's blunt family-finance rule: whoever won't provide for his own household is 'worse than an infidel.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: My son, if sinners _____ thee, consent thou not.
Pulpit Ready.verse: My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.
Pulpit Ready.note: Solomon's first fatherly warning is short and sweet: if sinners 'entice' thee, consent thou not.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited _____, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Whited sepulchres' — tombs painted bright white: gleaming outside, dead men's bones within. Jesus' sharpest woe.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of _____ toward God, and toward men.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul before Felix: his daily exercise is a conscience 'void of offence' — British spelling, with a c.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and _____, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
Pulpit Ready.note: The great supper's last invitation: go out to the highways and 'hedges' — anywhere — and fill the house.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And God sent me before you to preserve you a _____ in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And God sent me before you to preserve you a posterity in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
Pulpit Ready.note: Joseph to the brothers who sold him: God sent me ahead 'to preserve you a posterity' — providence reframing betrayal.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in _____ of me.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.
Pulpit Ready.note: The Lord's Supper words, as Paul received and passed them on: 'this do in remembrance of me.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that _____ by the stuff: they shall part alike.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.
Pulpit Ready.note: David's rule after Ziklag: those who guard the supplies share equally with those who fight. Every church's behind-the-scenes verse.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye _____ up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.
Pulpit Ready.note: Two men in white at the Ascension, gently: why stand ye 'gazing'? He'll come back the same way he left.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But when the _____ of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,
Pulpit Ready.verse: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,
Pulpit Ready.note: 'The fulness of the time' — God's clock struck, and his Son arrived. The KJV spells fulness with one l.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world _____ down are come hither also;
Pulpit Ready.verse: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;
Pulpit Ready.note: The Thessalonian mob's complaint became a compliment: these men 'have turned the world upside down.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: O foolish Galatians, who hath _____ you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?
Pulpit Ready.verse: O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?
Pulpit Ready.note: 'O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you?' — Paul at his most exasperated with a church he founded.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Ye who turn judgment to _____, and leave off righteousness in the earth,
Pulpit Ready.verse: Ye who turn judgment to wormwood, and leave off righteousness in the earth,
Pulpit Ready.note: Israel turned justice into 'wormwood' — bitter as gall. Amos soon calls for judgment to run down as waters (5:24).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the _____: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels were coming.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels were coming.
Pulpit Ready.note: Isaac went out 'to meditate in the field at the eventide' — and looked up to see Rebekah's camels coming.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I therefore so run, not as _____; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air:
Pulpit Ready.verse: I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air:
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul the athlete doesn't run 'uncertainly' or shadowbox — 'not as one that beateth the air.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the LORD said, I have _____ according to thy word:
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the LORD said, I have pardoned according to thy word:
Pulpit Ready.note: Moses interceded after the spies' bad report, and God answered in seven words: 'I have pardoned according to thy word.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: This know also, that in the last days _____ times shall come.
Pulpit Ready.verse: This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Perilous times' in the last days — then Paul lists them: lovers of self, lovers of money, lovers of pleasure.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Beside me there is no saviour' — the KJV keeps the British u, and God keeps the title for himself.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The righteous shall _____ like the palm tree: he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
Pulpit Ready.note: The righteous 'flourish like the palm tree' — and two verses later they're still bearing fruit in old age.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He that _____ his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.
Pulpit Ready.note: Cover-up versus confession: hide your sins and you won't prosper; confess and forsake them and you'll find mercy.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And as it is _____ unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:
Pulpit Ready.verse: And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:
Pulpit Ready.note: One life, one death, then judgment — and verse 28 adds the good news: Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many _____ proofs, being seen of them forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God:
Pulpit Ready.verse: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God:
Pulpit Ready.note: Forty days of 'many infallible proofs' — Luke's case that the risen Jesus was no rumor.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Draught' (not draft) is a haul of fish. Peter had caught nothing all night — then the nets started breaking.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.
Pulpit Ready.note: Forgive the repentant brother, says Paul, so Satan gains no advantage: 'we are not ignorant of his devices.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no _____, the strife ceaseth.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
Pulpit Ready.note: No wood, no fire; no 'talebearer,' no strife. Starve gossip of fuel and quarrels go out on their own.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Abstain from all _____ of evil.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Abstain from all appearance of evil.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Abstain from all appearance of evil' — one of the shortest commands in Paul's rapid-fire closing list.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or _____, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.
Pulpit Ready.verse: That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.
Pulpit Ready.note: Christ's goal for his bride, the church: 'not having spot, or wrinkle' — no stain, no crease.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Blessed be the LORD my strength, which _____ my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Blessed be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:
Pulpit Ready.note: David the warrior-poet credits God with his combat skills: he 'teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and _____ of heart,
Pulpit Ready.verse: And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart,
Pulpit Ready.note: The first church: daily together, breaking bread house to house, with 'gladness and singleness of heart.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For ever, O LORD, thy word is _____ in heaven.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.
Pulpit Ready.note: In a world of revisions, one thing is final: 'For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Now therefore so shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I took thee from the _____, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Now therefore so shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:
Pulpit Ready.note: God reminded King David where he started: 'I took thee from the sheepcote' — from following sheep to ruling Israel.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of _____: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jesus' prelude to the parable of the rich fool: a man's life 'consisteth not' in the abundance of his possessions.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast _____;
Pulpit Ready.verse: When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained;
Pulpit Ready.note: David looked up at the moon and stars God had 'ordained' and asked, 'What is man?' Stargazing as theology.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of _____ springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled;
Pulpit Ready.note: A 'root of bitterness' springs up and defiles many — Hebrews borrowing an image from Deuteronomy 29:18.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And there were four _____ men at the entering in of the gate: and they said one to another, Why sit we here until we die?
Pulpit Ready.verse: And there were four leprous men at the entering in of the gate: and they said one to another, Why sit we here until we die?
Pulpit Ready.note: Four 'leprous' men at Samaria's gate asked the question that saved a starving city: 'Why sit we here until we die?'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an _____ evil, full of deadly poison.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.
Pulpit Ready.note: Mankind has tamed beasts, birds, and sea creatures (verse 7), but the tongue 'can no man tame.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He shall see of the _____ of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied' — birth-pain language for the harvest of the cross.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and _____ is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, he hath also rejected thee from being king.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, he hath also rejected thee from being king.
Pulpit Ready.note: Samuel to Saul: rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and 'stubbornness' as idolatry. Disobedience is never small.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the _____ of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world:
Pulpit Ready.verse: That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world:
Pulpit Ready.note: Before Christ, Gentiles were 'aliens from the commonwealth of Israel' — outsiders now 'made nigh' (verse 13).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing _____, gravity, sincerity,
Pulpit Ready.verse: In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity,
Pulpit Ready.note: Titus' teaching checklist: 'uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity' — integrity nobody can bribe.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy tranquillity.
Pulpit Ready.note: Daniel's counsel to a proud king: break off your sins by showing mercy to the poor, and perhaps your 'tranquillity' will last.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Let all things be done _____ and in order.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Let all things be done decently and in order.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's closing rule for Corinth's chaotic worship services: 'decently and in order.' Church business meetings agree.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven _____ violence, and the violent take it by force.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.
Pulpit Ready.note: One of Jesus' most debated sayings: the kingdom 'suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Thou tellest my _____: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
Pulpit Ready.verse: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
Pulpit Ready.note: God tallies every one of David's 'wanderings' and keeps his tears in a bottle — the most tender filing system in Scripture.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Moreover, because I have set my _____ to the house of my God, I have of mine own proper good, of gold and silver, which I have given to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house,
Pulpit Ready.verse: Moreover, because I have set my affection to the house of my God, I have of mine own proper good, of gold and silver, which I have given to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house,
Pulpit Ready.note: David gave his own treasure for the temple 'because I have set my affection to the house of my God.' Giving follows the heart.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Of the Rock that begat thee thou art _____, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.
Pulpit Ready.note: In Moses' song, God is 'the Rock that begat thee' — and Israel was 'unmindful' of him. Forgetting is a spiritual act.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: As a jewel of gold in a swine's snout, so is a fair woman which is without _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: As a jewel of gold in a swine's snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.
Pulpit Ready.note: Proverbs' most memorable image: beauty without 'discretion' is a gold ring in a pig's snout.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor _____; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.
Pulpit Ready.note: The Servant had 'no form nor comeliness' — nothing in his looks to draw a crowd.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Art thou he that _____ Israel?
Pulpit Ready.verse: And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
Pulpit Ready.note: Ahab greeted Elijah as 'he that troubleth Israel'; Elijah shot back that Ahab was the real troubler (18:18).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, _____ thou what thou readest?
Pulpit Ready.verse: And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?
Pulpit Ready.note: Philip runs alongside the Ethiopian's chariot and opens with the best question in evangelism history.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and _____ as an army with banners?
Pulpit Ready.verse: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
Pulpit Ready.note: The beloved, fair as the moon and clear as the sun, is 'terrible as an army with banners' — awe-inspiring, not awful.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Let us hear the _____ of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
Pulpit Ready.note: After twelve chapters of 'vanity,' the Preacher's bottom line: fear God, keep his commandments — the whole duty of man.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For whom the LORD loveth he _____; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For whom the LORD loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.
Pulpit Ready.note: Correction as a love language: 'whom the LORD loveth he correcteth' — as a father the son he delights in.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I _____ my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jesus' last words in Luke echo Psalm 31:5: 'into thy hands I commend my spirit.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Therefore, behold, I will _____ her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her.
Pulpit Ready.note: God's plan for wayward Israel: 'I will allure her' into the wilderness and 'speak comfortably unto her.' Divine courtship.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I know both how to be _____, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.
Pulpit Ready.verse: I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's contentment covered both extremes: 'abased' and abounding, full and hungry.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the LORD said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a _____ people:
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the LORD said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:
Pulpit Ready.note: After the golden calf, God's verdict on Israel: 'a stiffnecked people' — like oxen refusing to bow to the yoke.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Wisdom is the _____ thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Wisdom is the principal thing' — principal, not principle: the chief thing. So get it, whatever it costs.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the LORD will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the LORD will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rereward.
Pulpit Ready.note: No need to flee in panic: the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your 'rereward' — your rear guard. Covered both ways.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the _____ was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul and Barnabas split over John Mark — a 'contention' so sharp they sailed separate ways.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without _____, save in his own country, and in his own house.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.
Pulpit Ready.note: Back home in Nazareth the hometown crowd took offence — and the KJV keeps the British u in 'honour.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And, behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you: but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be _____ with power from on high.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And, behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you: but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Tarry ye' and wait to be 'endued with power from on high' — a promise kept at Pentecost in Acts 2.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Who is this that _____ counsel by words without knowledge?
Pulpit Ready.verse: Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?
Pulpit Ready.note: God finally answers Job out of the whirlwind, and opens with a question: 'Who is this that darkeneth counsel?'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent _____ me, and I did eat.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.
Pulpit Ready.note: The first passing of the buck: Adam blamed the woman, and the woman blamed the serpent that 'beguiled' her.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Speak ye _____ to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD'S hand double for all her sins.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD'S hand double for all her sins.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem' — literally 'speak to the heart.' Handel's Messiah opens with these very lines.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But there is _____ with thee, that thou mayest be feared.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But there is forgiveness with thee, that thou mayest be feared.
Pulpit Ready.note: Forgiveness doesn't make God casual; it makes him 'feared.' A song of ascents prayed 'out of the depths' (130:1).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Only be thou strong and very _____, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper whithersoever thou goest.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper whithersoever thou goest.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Be strong and of a good courage' appears in 1:6 and 1:9 — but 1:7 turns it up: 'very courageous.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with _____, that thou mayest see.
Pulpit Ready.verse: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see.
Pulpit Ready.note: Laodicea thought itself rich; Jesus prescribes tried gold, white raiment, and 'eyesalve' so they can finally see.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all _____ of no value.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.
Pulpit Ready.note: Job to his three counselors: 'ye are all physicians of no value' — bad doctors with worse bedside manner.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I press toward the _____ for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
Pulpit Ready.verse: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'I press toward the mark' — Paul as a runner leaning toward the finish line, eyes off the past.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he shall be unto thee a _____ of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him.
Pulpit Ready.note: The women of Bethlehem to once-bitter Naomi about her new grandson: 'a restorer of thy life' — and Ruth better than seven sons.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a _____?
Pulpit Ready.verse: And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause?
Pulpit Ready.note: Eliab mocked his kid brother on the battlefield; David answered, 'Is there not a cause?' — then went out to face Goliath.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: A _____ woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.
Pulpit Ready.verse: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.
Pulpit Ready.note: Long before the famous chapter 31, Proverbs already calls 'a virtuous woman' a crown to her husband.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Blotting out the _____ of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross;
Pulpit Ready.note: 'The handwriting of ordinances' that stood against us — blotted out, taken away, and nailed to the cross.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Both riches and honour come of thee, and thou _____ over all; and in thine hand is power and might; and in thine hand it is to make great, and to give strength unto all.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Both riches and honour come of thee, and thou reignest over all; and in thine hand is power and might; and in thine hand it is to make great, and to give strength unto all.
Pulpit Ready.note: From David's last great public prayer: riches and honour come of thee, and 'thou reignest over all.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's one-line parenting rule: don't provoke your children, 'lest they be discouraged.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: How doth the city sit _____, that was full of people! how is she become as a widow! she that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become tributary!
Pulpit Ready.verse: How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people! how is she become as a widow! she that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become tributary!
Pulpit Ready.note: Lamentations opens with a gasp: how doth the city sit 'solitary' — once full of people, now like a widow.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For the love of Christ _____ us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead:
Pulpit Ready.verse: For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead:
Pulpit Ready.note: 'The love of Christ constraineth us' — hems us in and drives us on. Paul's motive for everything.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be _____ from thee.
Pulpit Ready.verse: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.
Pulpit Ready.note: Job's final confession: God can do every thing, and 'no thought can be withholden from thee.' The questions finally rest.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The _____ head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'The hoary head is a crown of glory' — grey hair as a medal, if it's earned on the road of righteousness.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: To speak evil of no man, to be no _____, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.
Pulpit Ready.verse: To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.
Pulpit Ready.note: Speak evil of no man, be no 'brawlers' — Paul's civility code for the believers on Crete.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Among all this people there were seven hundred chosen men _____; every one could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Among all this people there were seven hundred chosen men lefthanded; every one could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss.
Pulpit Ready.note: Seven hundred 'lefthanded' Benjamites could sling a stone at a hair and not miss. Ehud was a lefthanded Benjamite too (3:15).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He _____ not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God;
Pulpit Ready.verse: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God;
Pulpit Ready.note: Abraham, about a hundred years old, 'staggered not at the promise' — no wobble, just stronger faith.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he made in Jerusalem engines, invented by cunning men, to be on the towers and upon the bulwarks, to shoot arrows and great stones withal. And his name spread far abroad; for he was _____ helped, till he was strong.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he made in Jerusalem engines, invented by cunning men, to be on the towers and upon the bulwarks, to shoot arrows and great stones withal. And his name spread far abroad; for he was marvellously helped, till he was strong.
Pulpit Ready.note: King Uzziah was 'marvellously helped, till he was strong' — and the next verse says his heart was lifted up. Strength became his snare.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Brethren, I count not myself to have _____: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,
Pulpit Ready.verse: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul admits he hasn't 'apprehended' — laid hold of — the prize yet. So: forget what's behind and reach forward.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the _____ waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.
Pulpit Ready.note: The 'husbandman' is a farmer, not a spouse — and he waits patiently for the early and latter rain.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of _____ shall come from the presence of the Lord;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord;
Pulpit Ready.note: Peter at Solomon's porch, right after the lame man walked: repent, and 'times of refreshing' will come.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: A land wherein thou shalt eat bread without _____, thou shalt not lack any thing in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass.
Pulpit Ready.verse: A land wherein thou shalt eat bread without scarceness, thou shalt not lack any thing in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass.
Pulpit Ready.note: The promised land's brochure: bread without 'scarceness,' stones of iron, hills of brass. Then Moses warns: don't forget the Giver.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Keeping mercy for thousands, _____ iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.
Pulpit Ready.note: Part of God's self-portrait on Sinai: keeping mercy for thousands, 'forgiving' iniquity and transgression and sin.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: How shall we escape, if we _____ so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
Pulpit Ready.verse: How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
Pulpit Ready.note: Hebrews' first warning: the danger isn't rejecting so great salvation outright — it's simply to 'neglect' it.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.
Pulpit Ready.note: After wrestling till daybreak, Jacob limped away amazed: he had seen God face to face, and his life was 'preserved.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God _____!
Pulpit Ready.verse: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!
Pulpit Ready.note: Hired to curse Israel, Balaam blessed instead: 'What hath God wrought!' — later the first message on Morse's telegraph line, 1844.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye _____ worship, him declare I unto you.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.
Pulpit Ready.note: On Mars' hill, Paul turns Athens' altar 'TO THE UNKNOWN GOD' into his sermon opener.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, _____ you like men, be strong.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Quit you like men' is old English for 'conduct yourselves' — act like grown-ups. It doesn't mean give up!

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their restingplace.
Pulpit Ready.note: God's people became lost sheep, led astray by their shepherds, until they forgot their 'restingplace.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And my speech and my preaching was not with _____ words of man's wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power:
Pulpit Ready.verse: And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man's wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power:
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's preaching in Corinth: no 'enticing words' of clever rhetoric, just a demonstration of the Spirit and power.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the _____ plant of a strange vine unto me?
Pulpit Ready.verse: Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?
Pulpit Ready.note: God planted 'a noble vine, wholly a right seed' — how did it turn into the 'degenerate plant of a strange vine'?

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made _____ for the transgressors.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
Pulpit Ready.note: Isaiah 53 ends in prayer: numbered with the transgressors, he 'made intercession' for them — as Jesus did on the cross (Luke 23:34).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Then had the churches rest throughout all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria, and were _____; and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Then had the churches rest throughout all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified; and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied.
Pulpit Ready.note: After Saul's conversion the churches had rest and were 'edified' — built up — and multiplied.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the _____ to know his place;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place;
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Hast thou commanded the morning?' God asks Job. Zacharias later calls Jesus 'the dayspring from on high' (Luke 1:78).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall _____ come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.
Pulpit Ready.verse: He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.
Pulpit Ready.note: The verse behind the hymn 'Bringing in the Sheaves': tearful sowers 'shall doubtless come again with rejoicing.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the _____ of the heart the mouth speaketh.
Pulpit Ready.verse: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jesus' diagnosis of speech: the mouth only says what the heart is overflowing with — out of its 'abundance.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our _____; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
Pulpit Ready.note: Our high priest isn't distant: he is 'touched with the feeling of our infirmities' — tempted in all points, yet without sin.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And Moses spake unto Aaron, Say unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, Come near before the LORD: for he hath heard your _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And Moses spake unto Aaron, Say unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, Come near before the LORD: for he hath heard your murmurings.
Pulpit Ready.note: Israel grumbled for bread, and God heard every one of their 'murmurings' — then answered with manna anyway.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: _____ not as I will, but as thou wilt.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.
Pulpit Ready.note: Gethsemane's hinge word: 'nevertheless not as I will' — the prayer that turned the night toward the cross.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: _____ to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Endeavouring' — British u and all — to keep the unity of the Spirit. Unity is kept, not manufactured.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.
Pulpit Ready.note: Aaron ran with his censer and 'stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.' Intercession on the run.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Yet there shall be a space between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure: come not near unto it, that ye may know the way by which ye must go: for ye have not passed this way _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Yet there shall be a space between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure: come not near unto it, that ye may know the way by which ye must go: for ye have not passed this way heretofore.
Pulpit Ready.note: Follow the ark and keep your distance so you can see the way — 'for ye have not passed this way heretofore.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Set thee up _____, make thee high heaps: set thine heart toward the highway, even the way which thou wentest: turn again, O virgin of Israel, turn again to these thy cities.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Set thee up waymarks, make thee high heaps: set thine heart toward the highway, even the way which thou wentest: turn again, O virgin of Israel, turn again to these thy cities.
Pulpit Ready.note: Exiles were told to 'set thee up waymarks' on the road out of Israel — so they could find their way back home.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my _____, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower.
Pulpit Ready.note: David stacks up names for God in one breath — rock, fortress, deliverer, high tower — and 'buckler,' a small round shield.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And when he had removed him, he raised up unto them David to be their king; to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall _____ all my will.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And when he had removed him, he raised up unto them David to be their king; to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul quoting God on David: 'a man after mine own heart' — and the KJV spells fulfil with just one l.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Not _____ in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord' — Paul's whole work ethic in nine words.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, _____; and some, pastors and teachers;
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers;
Pulpit Ready.note: Christ's gifts to the church: apostles, prophets, 'evangelists,' pastors and teachers — for perfecting the saints.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made _____:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck:
Pulpit Ready.note: Some 'made shipwreck' of their faith — and Paul, who'd been shipwrecked three times (2 Corinthians 11:25), knew the image.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: It is like the precious _____ upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments;
Pulpit Ready.verse: It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments;
Pulpit Ready.note: Unity is like anointing oil on Aaron's head, running down his beard to his robe — fragrant, generous, holy.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an _____ of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.
Pulpit Ready.note: The Philippians' gift, carried by Epaphroditus, was 'an odour of a sweet smell' — the KJV spells it British.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Because _____ against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
Pulpit Ready.note: When the 'sentence' against an evil work is delayed, hearts fill with nerve to do more. Justice delayed emboldens.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and _____ the girdle of his reins.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins.
Pulpit Ready.note: The coming Branch of Jesse wears righteousness and 'faithfulness' as his belt — character worn as clothing.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a _____, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
Pulpit Ready.note: The high priest's gold plate was engraved like 'a signet' with a four-word motto: HOLINESS TO THE LORD.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: So we _____ in the work: and half of them held the spears from the rising of the morning till the stars appeared.
Pulpit Ready.verse: So we laboured in the work: and half of them held the spears from the rising of the morning till the stars appeared.
Pulpit Ready.note: Half held spears while half built, from dawn till the stars appeared. Nehemiah's wall rose with trowels and swords.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The voice said, Cry. And he said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the _____ thereof is as the flower of the field:
Pulpit Ready.verse: The voice said, Cry. And he said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field:
Pulpit Ready.note: 'All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower' — Peter quotes it in 1 Peter 1:24.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For the LORD your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which _____ not persons, nor taketh reward:
Pulpit Ready.verse: For the LORD your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward:
Pulpit Ready.note: The great, mighty, terrible God 'regardeth not persons' — no favoritism, no bribes. Peter learned it again in Acts 10:34.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: _____ one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Forbearing one another' — putting up with each other — and forgiving, even as Christ forgave you.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man _____ and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
Pulpit Ready.note: Joseph's advice to Pharaoh: find a man 'discreet and wise' — and Pharaoh promptly decided Joseph was that man (41:39).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I exhort therefore, that, first of all, _____, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men;
Pulpit Ready.verse: I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men;
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's prayer list for Timothy: 'supplications, prayers, intercessions,' and thanks — for all men, kings included.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And now for a little space grace hath been shewed from the LORD our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a nail in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and give us a little _____ in our bondage.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And now for a little space grace hath been shewed from the LORD our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a nail in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and give us a little reviving in our bondage.
Pulpit Ready.note: Ezra's prayer counts small mercies: a remnant, a nail in the holy place, and 'a little reviving in our bondage.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be _____:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:
Pulpit Ready.note: Peter's checklist for church life ends small and practical: 'be pitiful, be courteous.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Again, When a righteous man doth turn from his righteousness, and commit iniquity, and I lay a _____ before him, he shall die: because thou hast not given him warning, he shall die in his sin, and his righteousness which he hath done shall not be remembered; but his blood will I require at thine hand.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Again, When a righteous man doth turn from his righteousness, and commit iniquity, and I lay a stumblingblock before him, he shall die: because thou hast not given him warning, he shall die in his sin, and his righteousness which he hath done shall not be remembered; but his blood will I require at thine hand.
Pulpit Ready.note: Ezekiel the watchman learns the stakes: if he fails to warn the backslider, God will require that blood at his hand.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a _____ were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jesus' fierce protectiveness of little ones: better a 'millstone' round the neck than to make one of them stumble.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Thou, O LORD, _____ for ever; thy throne from generation to generation.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Thou, O LORD, remainest for ever; thy throne from generation to generation.
Pulpit Ready.note: Lamentations ends among ruins, but this verse stands: 'Thou, O LORD, remainest for ever; thy throne from generation to generation.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And one of his servants said, None, my lord, O king: but Elisha, the prophet that is in Israel, telleth the king of Israel the words that thou speakest in thy _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And one of his servants said, None, my lord, O king: but Elisha, the prophet that is in Israel, telleth the king of Israel the words that thou speakest in thy bedchamber.
Pulpit Ready.note: Syria's king suspected a spy; his servant explained that Elisha told Israel's king even what was said 'in thy bedchamber.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Ye said also, Behold, what a _____ is it! and ye have snuffed at it, saith the LORD of hosts; and ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick; thus ye brought an offering: should I accept this of your hand? saith the LORD.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Ye said also, Behold, what a weariness is it! and ye have snuffed at it, saith the LORD of hosts; and ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick; thus ye brought an offering: should I accept this of your hand? saith the LORD.
Pulpit Ready.note: Israel's priests sniffed at worship — 'what a weariness is it!' — then offered God the torn, the lame, and the sick.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and _____ the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
Pulpit Ready.note: God's first words to humankind were a blessing with a commission attached: multiply, 'replenish' the earth, and subdue it.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall _____ as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass:
Pulpit Ready.verse: My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass:
Pulpit Ready.note: Moses' farewell song opens softly: 'my speech shall distil as the dew' — and the KJV spells it with a single l.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But Mary kept all these things, and _____ them in her heart.
Pulpit Ready.verse: But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
Pulpit Ready.note: After the shepherds' visit, Mary kept it all and 'pondered' — turned it over and over — in her heart.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Casting down _____, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ;
Pulpit Ready.note: Spiritual warfare, Pauline style: casting down 'imaginations' and taking every thought captive.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and _____ the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
Pulpit Ready.verse: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
Pulpit Ready.note: Jesus on discipleship: a wise builder sits down and 'counteth the cost' before laying a single stone.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Thanks be unto God for his _____ gift.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul ends two chapters about giving money by pointing to the one gift words can't describe — 'unspeakable.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Wherefore doth a living man _____, a man for the punishment of his sins?
Pulpit Ready.verse: Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?
Pulpit Ready.note: The same chapter that sings 'great is thy faithfulness' asks why a living man should 'complain' about the punishment of his sins.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia: for the Lord God _____ reigneth.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth' — the words Handel set in the Hallelujah Chorus of Messiah.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou _____ in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.
Pulpit Ready.note: The psalmist preaches to himself: why art thou cast down, why 'disquieted'? Hope thou in God. The refrain returns in 42:11 and 43:5.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set _____ against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah; and they were smitten.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah; and they were smitten.
Pulpit Ready.note: Jehoshaphat sent singers ahead of the army; 'when they began to sing,' the LORD set 'ambushments.' Worship as battle plan.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For I _____ not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul arrived in Corinth 'determined' to know nothing among them but Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great _____, and sin against God?
Pulpit Ready.verse: There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
Pulpit Ready.note: Joseph to Potiphar's wife: not 'I might get caught' but 'how can I sin against God?' — integrity in one question.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And be not drunk with wine, wherein is _____; but be filled with the Spirit;
Pulpit Ready.verse: And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit;
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's contrast: don't be filled with wine, which leads to 'excess' — be filled with the Spirit instead.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Seest thou a man _____ in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
Pulpit Ready.note: See a man 'diligent' in his business? He'll stand before kings — Joseph and Daniel could testify.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I make a decree, That in every dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel: for he is the living God, and _____ for ever, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed, and his dominion shall be even unto the end.
Pulpit Ready.verse: I make a decree, That in every dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel: for he is the living God, and stedfast for ever, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed, and his dominion shall be even unto the end.
Pulpit Ready.note: After the lions' den, King Darius decreed that Daniel's God is 'the living God, and stedfast for ever' — no 'a' in the KJV.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I have _____ out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.
Pulpit Ready.verse: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions' — sins gone like a cloud burned away by the sun.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of _____ between us;
Pulpit Ready.verse: For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us;
Pulpit Ready.note: 'The middle wall of partition' between Jew and Gentile — broken down by Christ, who 'is our peace.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are _____; but the things which are not seen are eternal.
Pulpit Ready.verse: While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Temporal' means lasting only for a time — Paul's reason to fix your eyes on the unseen, which is eternal.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: There is therefore now no _____ to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
Pulpit Ready.verse: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
Pulpit Ready.note: After Romans 7's wrestling, chapter 8 opens with the verdict: 'no condemnation' for those in Christ Jesus.
