Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not _____ their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.
Pulpit Ready.verse: To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.
Pulpit Ready.note: God was in Christ reconciling the world, 'not imputing' — not charging — their trespasses unto them.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: The discretion of a man _____ his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
Pulpit Ready.verse: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'The discretion of a man deferreth his anger' — and it is his glory to pass over an offence. Patience as honour.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For consider him that endured such _____ of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.
Pulpit Ready.note: When you're weary, consider Jesus, who 'endured such contradiction of sinners' — hostility — against himself.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Yet all this _____ me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Yet all this availeth me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate.
Pulpit Ready.note: Haman had riches, sons, and royal favour, yet it all 'availeth me nothing' while Mordecai sat at the gate. Envy spoils the feast.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Till I come, give _____ to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's job description for young Timothy until he arrives: give 'attendance to reading,' exhortation, doctrine.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as _____ between thine eyes.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes.
Pulpit Ready.note: Bind God's words on your hand and as 'frontlets between thine eyes' — the root of the phylacteries mentioned in Matthew 23:5.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And it fell on a day, that Elisha passed to Shunem, where was a great woman; and she _____ him to eat bread. And so it was, that as oft as he passed by, he turned in thither to eat bread.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And it fell on a day, that Elisha passed to Shunem, where was a great woman; and she constrained him to eat bread. And so it was, that as oft as he passed by, he turned in thither to eat bread.
Pulpit Ready.note: The Shunammite woman 'constrained' Elisha to eat — then furnished him a little chamber on the wall (4:10). Hospitality with a plan.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth _____, and where thieves break through and steal:
Pulpit Ready.verse: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:
Pulpit Ready.note: Earthly treasure has two enemies, says Jesus: moth for the cloth and rust for the metal — both 'doth corrupt.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Beautiful for _____, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Beautiful for situation' — Zion praised for its setting, the KJV's stately way of saying 'great location.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he said, Be it far from me, O LORD, that I should do this: is not this the blood of the men that went in _____ of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mighty men.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he said, Be it far from me, O LORD, that I should do this: is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mighty men.
Pulpit Ready.note: Three mighty men risked their lives for water from Bethlehem's well; David poured it out to the LORD rather than drink it.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Blessed be the Lord, who daily _____ us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. Selah.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. Selah.
Pulpit Ready.note: Not weekly, not monthly — the Lord 'daily loadeth us with benefits.' A cart that never comes back empty.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And Moses said unto the LORD, O my Lord, I am not _____, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And Moses said unto the LORD, O my Lord, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
Pulpit Ready.note: Moses' excuse at the bush: 'I am not eloquent' — and God answered, 'Who hath made man's mouth?' (4:11).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that _____ his lips is wise.
Pulpit Ready.verse: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.
Pulpit Ready.note: More words, more chances to sin — so the wise man 'refraineth his lips.' James 1:19 says the same: slow to speak.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a _____, and unto the Greeks foolishness;
Pulpit Ready.verse: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness;
Pulpit Ready.note: Christ crucified: to some a 'stumblingblock' — one word in the KJV — and to others sheer foolishness.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was _____ in his own eyes.
Pulpit Ready.verse: In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
Pulpit Ready.note: The refrain of Judges: no king in Israel, and 'every man did that which was right in his own eyes.' It closes the book too (21:25).

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Because thou servedst not the LORD thy God with _____, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things;
Pulpit Ready.verse: Because thou servedst not the LORD thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things;
Pulpit Ready.note: Moses warns of curses 'because thou servedst not the LORD thy God with joyfulness' — grudging service amid abundance.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Are not two sparrows sold for a _____? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.
Pulpit Ready.note: Two sparrows for a 'farthing' — cheap birds, yet not one falls without your Father. Verse 31: you're worth more.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O _____? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
Pulpit Ready.verse: So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
Pulpit Ready.note: Mid-storm, a pagan shipmaster had to wake the prophet: 'What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Therefore thou art _____, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul springs a trap: after condemning the pagan world in chapter 1, he turns on the judge — 'thou art inexcusable.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you _____, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's farewell charge to the Ephesian elders: feed the flock God 'purchased with his own blood.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Surely the Lord GOD will do nothing, but he revealeth his _____ unto his servants the prophets.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Surely the Lord GOD will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.
Pulpit Ready.note: The herdsman-prophet's assurance: the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing his 'secret' to his servants the prophets.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a _____ shalt thou be in the earth.
Pulpit Ready.verse: When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.
Pulpit Ready.note: Cain's sentence: 'a fugitive and a vagabond' — the ground that received Abel's blood would no longer yield to him.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all was vanity and _____ of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all was vanity and vexation of spirit, and there was no profit under the sun.
Pulpit Ready.note: Solomon surveyed every project he'd built and found it all 'vanity and vexation of spirit' — no profit under the sun.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is _____ up in victory.
Pulpit Ready.verse: So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul quotes Isaiah 25:8 at the resurrection chapter's climax: 'Death is swallowed up in victory.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Brethren, if a man be _____ in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.
Pulpit Ready.note: If someone is 'overtaken in a fault,' restore him gently — and check yourself while you're at it.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, _____ till I come.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Occupy till I come' — do business with what you've been given until the master returns.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name; worship the LORD in the beauty of _____.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name; worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness' — then Psalm 29 thunders the phrase 'the voice of the LORD' seven times.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and _____ of the Lord.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
Pulpit Ready.note: Fathers, don't provoke your children to wrath; raise them 'in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the _____ thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.
Pulpit Ready.note: The mountain before Zerubbabel becomes a plain, and the 'headstone' comes out with shouts of 'Grace, grace unto it.'

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the twelve gates were twelve pearls; every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were _____ glass.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the twelve gates were twelve pearls; every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass.
Pulpit Ready.note: Pearl gates, and a street of gold so pure it is 'as it were transparent glass.' Heaven's paving is see-through.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and _____ and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?
Pulpit Ready.verse: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?
Pulpit Ready.note: God's kindness isn't permission: his 'forbearance' and longsuffering are meant to lead you to repentance.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the _____ wherewith ye are called,
Pulpit Ready.verse: I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called,
Pulpit Ready.note: Writing as 'the prisoner of the Lord,' Paul urges a walk worthy of your 'vocation' — your calling.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Nay but, O man, who art thou that _____ against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?
Pulpit Ready.verse: Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?
Pulpit Ready.note: Paul's potter-and-clay rebuke — 'who art thou that repliest against God?' — echoes Isaiah 45:9.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall yet again take root _____, and bear fruit upward.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall yet again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.
Pulpit Ready.note: God's promise to Judah's remnant: 'take root downward, and bear fruit upward.' Growth starts underground.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and _____ in pain together until now.
Pulpit Ready.verse: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.
Pulpit Ready.note: All creation 'groaneth and travaileth' — in labor pains — waiting for the coming redemption.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the _____, support the weak, be patient toward all men.
Pulpit Ready.verse: Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Comfort the feebleminded' — the fainthearted. Warn some, comfort others, support the weak: care fits the person.

Pulpit Ready.label: Don't Play With Me
Pulpit Ready.prompt: And ye shall hear of wars and _____ of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
Pulpit Ready.verse: And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.
Pulpit Ready.note: 'Wars and rumours of wars' — British u — 'but the end is not yet.' Jesus' calm on the Mount of Olives.
